EventName: Sorry Honey, I've Gotta Work Late
EventNotes:
For race day registration you can register at this link for Tuesday 9/15

Race day reg here


 

Sorry Honey, I've gotta work late! 

REGISTRATION:
We encourage racers to register early.  We are offering series entry, at a discount, or you can sign up for individual event dates.

COURSE INFO:
All races will be located in Forest Hill Park, Richmond, VA. 

Cross course: the lap will be approximately one mile in length using a combination of surfaces that may include grass, blacktop and dirt.   What type of bike?  We don't care...race your cross, mountain or gravel bike. 

Lapped Rider:  If you are lapped you can continue to race, unlike some cyclo cross races. Once the race leader finishes the required number of laps, remaining riders will will be done once they complete their current lap.  The event will be scored by number of laps completed, then by time.

AWARDS: 
There will be series awards after 3rd race.  To be eligible for prizes, you must enter and race all three events.  

DISTANCE/TIME:
All races will be about 45 minutes.  Our goal is for the 1st pace overall to race close to 45 minutes.  All racers then will finish their current lap once the leader finishes. There will be a countdown lap count at the start/finish.  Lapped racers will not be removed from the course!  All racers will be able to continue to the finish of the event!

NUMBER OF LAPS:
Race organizers will determine numbers of laps based on average time per lap of leaders.  Once laps times are established there will be l lap counter counting down the laps.  This number will be reduced by 1 each time the leader crosses the line.  Note that the number can change by 2 if the leader passes you during any given lap. We will ring a bell for riders to signal "one to go". Historically, the winner completes 11 to 12 laps in the 45 minute window.

 

DONATION:
Donations will go to the local trail working groups (RVA MORE) earmarked to maintain the trails at Forest Hill Park.  Please donate a few bucks during registration.

RAIN OR WET CONDITIONS
To protect/secure our use of the park, we will postpone or cancel a race in the event of rain or wet conditions.  Don't let this prevent you from registering early.  We are happy to transfer fees to another runriderace event.

Course set up
I will be out at the course by early afternoon.  If you are able to come, shoot me an email letting me know you can come and your cell for contact.  We will probably need help right up to race start.

EventName: SAMBA Bash Rattling Creek Mountain Bike Festival
EventNotes:
SAMBA BASH Rattling Creek Mountain Bike Festival

September 17 - 20, 2026

THE BASH IS ON!

REGISTRATION FEE INCREASES BY $10 after SEPTEMBER 4.

The BASH at Muckelratz is a rain or shine non-competitive mountain bike weekend in the Weiser State Forest on the Rattling Creek Trail system. SAMBA holds the event to generate funding to pay for the upkeep and expansion of the Rattling Creek IMBA Epic. Be sure to click “SHOW ALL NOTES” and scroll to bottom of page to review all details!

 

CLICK HERE TO VOLUNTEER

WE NEED YOUR HELP! SEEKING VOLUNTEERS, RAFFLE DONATIONS, CASH SPONSORS, DEMO BIKES, MOBILE BIKE MECHANICS. Anyone who commits to volunteering during the event will receive a discount code! If interested in helping make this event a success, please use the link above to sign up through SignUp Genius or send an email to events@sambabiker.com. SAMBA Staff, please be sure to check your @samba.com email account for discount code, contact events@sambabiker.com if you did not receive code.

 

Event Details:

  • Rattling Creek is classic Central PA Rock Garden riding. This is not a beginner mountain biker event, but it is not a race either. The trails are challenging but great riding can be had for most ability groups.
  • For a map please visit: Rattling Creek Trail System. It is also recommended that you download the Trailforks Rattling Creek (IMBA Epic) route to your mobile device in advance.
  • Camping is primitive with portable toilets, outdoor shower facilities and no hook-ups. We have very limited electric connectivity if needed for medical devices. The camping is in and around the main field at camp and the roads in and out are not paved.
  • Win raffle items donated by our awesome sponsors (must be 18+ and CASH ONLY $$$)!
  • Quiet hours at the Camp are strictly from 11 PM to 8 AM. This isn't just a rule; it's a township ordinance put in place because of noise complaints from neighbors. Breaking this rule could result in fines or even the permanent closure of The BASH for next year.
  • Please pack out anything you bring in to help keep our costs down!
  • HELMETS and WAIVERS are required on all groups rides due to our insurance regulations.
  • The event is only canceled due to extreme weather so come prepared for whatever we have.

Additional FAQs:

  • Are there beginner rides in Rattling Creek? There really are no true beginner rides. All the trails are technical and have rock gardens, significant elevation changes, and no easy way out except to try and make the ride. There is often no cell service on most of the trails so you still have to make it out pretty far to even get support.
  • Do I need to register in advance? Pre-registration via BikeReg is preferred. Even if you want to wait until Friday or Saturday to register, please use BikeReg. We prefer not to have to deal with cash and having the correct amount of change on hand.
  • Why is there no family rate? Families are welcome to come, but the this event is all about riding the IMBA Epic Rattling Creek Trail System. Dinner on Saturday is included in the price as are the facilities and rental of the campground.
  • What is the Saturday dinner menu? We will be ordering pizzas with various toppings and subs from the local JoJo's.
  • What about breakfast? Free coffee and bagels available (until we run out) from 730-930am in bunkhouse on Fri and Sat morning (self-serve).
  • Where is the schedule of events? A schedule will be available at the SAMBA tent. Schedule is subject to change, so please verify the latest information on event day.
  • Is water available at camp or do I need to bring my own? Yes water is available at the bunkhouse.
  • What if I am arriving late in the evening? Please check-in the next morning at the SAMBA tent. You can park anywhere within Camp Muckelratz.
  • Are dogs allowed? Yes, well-behaved dogs are permitted ON LEASH! Please ensure your dog is not a nuisance and is not aggressive toward other dogs or people. Also, be responsible and pickup after your pet to keep the area clean for everyone.
  • Is camping permitted on Sunday night? We don't rent Camp Muckleratz past Sunday at 1pm, which is when everyone must leave Muckleratz. You may camp in the state forest at the free campsites, you just have to reserve them, see Weiser State Forest website.
  • What if I want to camp but don't plan on participating in SAMBA activites/rides? We ask that you still register and pay for admission to the event since we need to cover the cost of the campground and portable toilets. If you do not wish to pay the event fee, you may camp in the state forest at the free campsites, you just have to reserve them, see Weiser State Forest website.
  • Are generators allowed? No, generators are not allowed.
  • Are ground fires allowed? No, ground fires are not allowed.
  • What is the address of Camp Muckelratz? 801 Deitrich Rd, Halifax, PA 17032. GPS Coordinates: 40.5412856,-76.7773905
  • What is the address for Lykens Glen Park? Glen Park Rd, Lykens, PA 17048 GPS Coordinates: 40.5622509,-76.6990354
  • Where can I learn about future SAMBA Events, Group Rides, and Trail Work Days? Please be sure to follow us on Luma(click SAMBA Rider - Join and also the Follow button) to get updates about future events!
  • Where should I park if I'm coming for Saturday only and not camping overnight? You can park at the entrance to Camp Muckelratz, see picture below. If this parking area is full, you can also park at the Snowmobile Lot White Oak Rd, Halifax, PA 17032 GPS Coordinates: 40.544711, -76.758519.
For more information about the event… go somewhere else.

FAQ:

I've never ridden a mountain bike or I'm pretty new, can I come?

Absofreakinlutely! We invite ALL levels of riders to come and participate. When you sign up we have you fill out a questionnaire to place you in a group based on your skill level. We have had women start out in the beginner groups and now coming into year 3 we have seen them advance to the higher groups, which is super exciting!

If I need a bike can I rent one?

Yes! See above we're working with none other than the amazing Brown County Bikes!

Do I have to camp with everyone?

No you do not, you can stay wherever you like! We always give that option for people who want to camp on site with us but we are happy to give you other recommendations on places to stay - sometimes there are cabins or rooms on site as well! Guess what you can even stay in the same building as the bike shop - Brown County Bikes, check out Brown County Barn Burner. Contact them for availability because they've blocked rooms for our group!
You can also check out the Brown County Visitor's Center website to see all accommodation options.
https://www.browncounty.com/stay/

I'm coming with my friends will I be in the same group as them?

Maybe, maybe not. While you ride with your friends all the time at home you might be best suited to be in a different group as them for our camp. It is important for us to give you the best tools and skills you need to be successful to continue riding more confidently and comfortably. Our coaches and staff are professionally trained through PMBIA or ICP, we have organized and guided hundreds of people in the outdoors since 2014 so please trust our methods to place you in a group we feel you will most excel in. If you have concerns please let us know too!
There are times once you are in your group we may need to shift you to another group but we will discuss this with you beforehand.

I have a strict diet can you accommodate me?

We can cover vegetarian, gluten free. If you have sever allergies or other dietary restrictions we due recommend bringing your own food. While we wish we could accommodate every person's request many times we are in remote locations for our camps and the caterers or food options are very limited. If you have a strict diet please sign up for the meal plan at least 30 days out so we can communicate that to our caterer.

What is the refund policy?

If you have to cancel first you can always transfer your ticket to another camp (the following year) or coaching session with Kate or Danielle to be used within a year. 60 days out full refund after that we do not offer refunds due to paying for permits, insurance, coaches, meals, etc.

September 8-20th The 5th Annual Hodag Country Ramble
Two nights of swimming, camping, community, riding and revelry on our family's property outside of Rhinelander, Wisconsin in the heart of the beautiful Northwoods.

Registrants will receive: two nights of camping, 5th anniversary pin, dinner Saturday evening, and free beverages on Saturday night.

This is the land where I was born and raised and I'm incredibly excited to share it with our far flung cycling friends both old and new. Soaring trees, rolling hills, and beautiful lakes await you.

Route: A mix two track, gravel, and pavement. 26, 50, and 80 mile options. A gravel bike or hardtail mtb will work great.
Ride fast or take it slow, all options are valid. Route will wind its way through National Forest Land, private logging acreage, quiet pavement, and high quality gravel. There are convenience stores on the longer routes and a stocked mid-ride rest stop on the long loop.

Schedule: 
Thursday - Early Camping Opens 3pm - Limited Availability
Friday: Arrive, Bandit Cross, Riders Meeting, Market, Swimming - Gates open at Noon
Saturday: 9:00am Ride, 7pm Family Dinner, Refreshments, Party

Family Dinner: Hosted by Chef Adam Blake, there will be complimentary New Belgium Beer and La Croix. Vegan and Carnivore Options. DJ's and bonfire after dinner.  

Camping space on site will be limited to 180 people but there are tons of campsites, hotels and resorts in the area. Due to space and liability concerns only registered participants will be allowed to camp on site or be on the premises. If you wish to camp with non-registered folks please choose the without camping category and make your own arrangements.

Vending: Bring Bike parts, clothes, stuff you make etc, to sell at the market.

On Site Camping: You will be responsible for providing most of your meals and water, except for Saturday Night's Dinner. The best bet is to be as self sufficient as possible. We will provide porta potty's and hand washing stations.  

There will be spaces for both vehicle and tent camping, as space is limited we highly encourage carpooling if possible. There is a beautiful lake an easy walk from the property, or very short ride for swimming, washing up, and pumping water.

Due to the fact that our beloved pup Baroo is no longer with us we are welcoming other dogs this year, but please make sure they are on their best behavior and that you pickup all their droppings. The neighbor has chickens and if your dog causes issue, y'all will have to leave. 

This land is incredibly important to my family and we're very excited to share its magic with you. We humbly request that you treat the land with care and respect, please do not litter, or damage the trees. If you're planning on using a hammock, please make sure the trees you sling are at least 8" in diameter.

Join us for the second annual Woodly's Great Gravel Adventure on Saturday, September 19, 2026! 

About the Race
Woodly's Great Gravel Adventure is presented by the Mountain State Forest Festival, one of the largest and oldest festivals in West Virginia. This year's 88th annual event will be held September 26 - October 4. The MSFF is a real cultural landmark that showcases WV in all its autumn glory. Due to the changing fall leaves and the Mountain State Forest Festival, autumn is a great time to visit the Elkins area with family and friends. Visit Mountain State Forest Festival | Elkins, WV to see all that the MSFF has in entertainment, food, and events while in town for the ride!

The race will traverse through the beautiful Cheat-Potomac District of the Monongahela National Forest. Race headquarters will be stationed in Stuart Recreation Area nestled along the banks of the Shavers Fork River. Stuart Recreation Area is 7 miles east of Elkins and was built in 1937 by CCC labor. Known to locals as Stuart's Park, the area provides great hiking trails and excellent fishing.

Woodly's Great Gravel Adventure is part of the WV Gravel series. Please visit WVGS website www.wvgravelseries.com for rules and regulations.

The majority of the race will be on gravel roads with some rail trail and paved roads mixed in. 

 

Aid Stations
2 aid stations will be along the course. The short course will pass only one aid station.  The medium and long course will go by two.  We recommend bringing appropriate fuel and drinks. Please monitor the weather and dress accordingly. Elkins weather can range from hot to snow in the autumn season.

Package Pick-Up
Package pick-up will begin Saturday, September 19 at 8:00 AM at Stuart Recreation Area in the small pavilion. (we were in the large pavilion last year, the small pavilion is a little past the large in Stuarts Recreation Area).

The Start
All riders will begin at the Small Pavilion in Stuart Recreation Area and head out of the park to Forest Road 91 and turn left on Shaver Fork Road.  All riders will continue approximately 16 miles to the first aid station.   Long, medium, short and e bike riders will start at staggered times.  Long course rides will begin at the start finish line beside the small pavilion at 9:00 AM, Medium course will begin at 10:00 AM and Short course and e bikes at 10:30AM.

Short Course
Once leaving Stuarts Recreation Area the short Course will continue along Shavers fork road which runs beside the Shavers Fork of the Cheat River until reaching the the first aid station, approximately 16 miles.  At this point you will turn and go back to Stuart Recreation Area and the finish line following the Shavers Fork road for a total of 33 miles.  Tentative course is posted here. Click here for: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53598614?privacy_code=9FmkGxzNAnA49KPVGykAeBXJexGSZzAp 

Medium Course
The Medium Course will follow the short course until the first aide station.  At this intersection a sharp right turn will be made onto Forest Road 828 to enter the Fernow Experimental Forest.   At the intersection with Forest Road 709 a right turn will be made.  Then a slight right will be made onto Forest Road 701.  We will continue to 701 through the Fernow Forest until intersecting with Brooklyn Heights Road just East of the town of Parsons.  At this intersection a left turn will be make onto a paved road.   Brooklyn Heights Road will become Billings Avenue.  We will continue on Billings Avenue into the town of Parsons.   Billings Ave will become Railroad Ave and after a few blocks will intersect with River street.  A sharp right and then left will be made to put us on the Allegheny Highlands Rail Trail.   The Rail trail will take us through the Town of Parsons and then continue on the trail until intersecting Shavers Fork Road.  Take a left onto Shavers Fork Road.  Continue on Shavers Fork Road and it will become Clifton-Nail Run Road.  We will continue along Clifton-Nail run road until coming to the Second aid station.  At this point a left turn will be made to cross the river and intersect with Shavers Fork road.  Turn right onto Shavers Fork Road and continue to the finish line in Stuarts Park Recreation Area for a total of 48 miles.  The Course is posted here: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53599343?privacy_code=JCHJNuC8ct14apg3jiZSMLhraOVlulDk

Long Course
The Long Course will follow the short course and medium course into the Fernow Forest.  After traveling on forest road 701 for a short ways a right turn will be made onto forest road 324 towards McGowen Mountain.  We will travel about 7 miles to the Yellow Creek trail head and turn around to return to to Forest Road 701.  We will turn right off of 324 back onto 701 and continue on the Medium course route as seen above until reaching the second aide station.   At the second aid station the Long Course will turn right and continue on Clifton-Nail Run Road until turning left on Log Lick Run road (also known as Timbucktoo Road).  Log Lick Run will intersect with Stalnaker Run Road.  A left turn will be made onto Stalnaker road.  Continue on Stalnaker Run Road until coming to the “graffiti bridge.”  After crossing the bridge continue until taking a right onto Shavers Fork Road and continue to Stuarts Park Recreation area and the finish line for a total of 75 miles.  The Long Course is posted here: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55908392

 

 

 

 

E-Bike Route.

The E-bike route will begin at the Stuarts recreation area and head out of the park on Forest Road 91.  As soon we leave the park we will turn left onto Shaver Fork Road.  We will continue on the Shavers Fork road until reaching the “blue bridge” a left turn will be made onto Clifton-Nail Run Road.  Once crossing the bridge there will be an Aid Station.  Continue going straight until reaching Log Lick Run, at this intersection turn left.  Continue on until the intersection of Stalnaker Run Road.  A left turn will be made here.  Continuing on Stalnaker until the “Graffiti bridge," just after passing the bridge you will turn right back onto Shaver fork Road. This will bring you back to the start finish line in Stuarts Park.  The route is a total of 27 miles. Click here for:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56387987

 

All riders will receive a meal and t-shirt with registration and a ticket to the  Forest Festival Kickoff Party and Chili Cook-Of (scheduled from 4-8pm September 26th in Elkins).  Additional meals and t-shirts can be purchased. You must register before August 28th to get a T-shirt.

Prizes
First, second, and third finishers for male and female open riders for the long course will receive a cash prize. All winners from each category will have prize table selection.  

Lodging and Camping
Stuart Recreation Area has individual camping sites that must be reserved for tents and campers. Reservations can be made at Recreation.gov Stuart Recreation Area, Monongahela National Forest - Recreation.gov

A group campsite that accommodates 40 people tent camping is also available. This site is available first come, first serve Friday, September 18 and Saturday, September 19 for $5.00 and can be paid for day of event.

Bear Heaven Recreation Area, known by locals as Bear Haven, is a few miles away from Stuart Recreation Area, and has campsites available first come, first serve for $5.00

Amanda and David Sheek invite you to Mammoth Lakes, the gateway to mountain adventure, for a gravel event and adventure festival to challenge the toughest of riders. The fifth annual Mammoth TUFF will take place September 19, 2026, and offers three distances so you can explore your version of TUFF. The short and medium courses will circle the famous caldera while the long course will travel through the Volcanic Tableland formed by the eruption thousands of years ago. The event is hosted by the Village at Mammoth Lakes and is part of the UCI Gravel World Series for 2026.
 

Guide: Click here to access the '26 guide 

The 2026 TUFF GUIDE is published as of Aug 25. Updated Sept 11.

Policy: 
No refunds. However, should the event be canceled due to adverse weather, natural catastrophe (forest fires included), or terrorism that threatens the safety of riders, a full refund will be issued to riders. 
Transfers allowed. Participants can transfer their registration to another participant for a $10 surcharge. 
BikeReg offers the Allianz Registration Protection to participants when checking out. This Allianz Registration Protector gives you an opportunity to get reimbursed for up to 100% of your entry if you can’t attend the event for a qualifying reason. We recommend purchasing insurance for your protection. 

Course/Routes:

Final routes will be released on the week of the event (~Sept 14). Due to the success of the ‘25 routes, you can expect the ’26 routes to be very similar. We are giving ourselves the flexibility to tweak the routes until the week of the event due to road conditions and safety factors. 
We encourage self-sufficiency with this event; however, there will be sufficient supplies and support at aid stations. Courses will be marked, but we suggest you have a computer or phone with nagivating capabilities. 

UCI Gravel World Series:

UCI Gravel World Championship qualifier categories are noted in the registration categories and those Age Groups are defined by the rider’s age on December 31, 2026. Riders in the elite category must hold a UCI license and provide the UCI ID when registering. NO license is required for the UCI Age Group categories; however, riders who qualify for the UCI Gravel World Championships and choose to race must hold a valid license issued by USA Cycling for that race. Our event grants qualification rights for the UCI Gravel World Championships for those riders finishing in the top 3 of each official category as well as those finishing in the top 25% of each official category.
Elite riders and younger age groups (19-49) will ride the TUFFEST course.
Older age groups (50-84) will ride the TUFFER course.

Adaptive TUFF:

We have Para Categories for the Short course and we will continue to run the Adaptive TUFF distance as an official route. Select Para Hand Cycle or Para Traditional Cycle in the custom questions during registration for the Adaptive Category. 

TUFF Stuff:

Registrations before July 14, 2026 at 11pm PST are guaranteed a free shirt. All registrations after July 14 will have the option to purchase merchandise from a limited inventory. Thanks for understanding and helping our order process.

If you want to order the 2026 shirt for pick-up at registration because you registered too late, you can order from our excess inventory here: https://tuffaf.net/

EventNotes:
No Pain, No Chain 
Chainless Downhill Race on Paper Route  
September 27, 2025 
 
Get ready for a unique test of skill and strategy at the No Pain, No Chain, a chainless downhill race that challenges riders to rely entirely on momentum and technique. All participants must remove their bike chains before racing, making this an event where pumping, cornering, and line choice are more important than ever. With a couple of punchy uphill sections sprinkled in, racers will have to think fast: stay on the bike or jump off and run? 
 
Timing:  
The course will be open for practice runs during the first two hours of the day, followed by timed race runs in the afternoon. Participants may complete up to three timed runs between 12:00 and 3:00 PM, with their fastest time counting toward the final results. 
Open Practice: 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM 
Timed Race Runs: 12:00 PM – 3:00 PM  
Awards Ceremony: 3:30 PM 
 
Race Categories:  
Open/Expert (Any Age M&F) 
10 and under (M&F) 
11-18 (M&F)

Course Description:  
The course will utilize the blue square downhill trail called “Paper Route” and a newly opened trail, “Return to Sender”. These trails combine for 1.3 miles and are a mix of machine-built flow features and more natural technical sections. The trail takes riders from the top of American Express over to the bottom of the Sun Bowl lift, under the Snowbridge, before making its way to the base area.

The Red Bird Crest 80K and 40k will  feature an epic course with lots of rocky features, single track, climbs, and amazing descents. This course will challenge your physical fitness and your bike handling. 

Course description 80k- updated 9-7

The 80k course will storm out of the Peabody Trail Head onto Hwy 66 then onto Double Creek Rd. The first major climb comes quick as you climb out of the river bottoms to the ridge. A gravel road will take us to the top of what's called Trace Branch. The summit of this climb is at about ~mile 4.5 of the race. You will cross the ridge and descend into a deep valley. This trail section can become pretty wet depending on rainfall for the area. This section will have you crossing slick creeks and rocks. it will be very fast as it has a downhill grade for ~4 miles. The first SAG station comes at mile 7. General bike tools water and race snacks, will be available. A short stretch of road will take you to the Crest Trail. Here you will begin a long steady climb back up to the ridge top. Once there, you will enjoy some good flowy trail. This is where the race will be won or lost. This long flat ridge will allow you to push the pace and build your lead or close the gap on the strong climbers in the field. A steep descent into SAG station 2 marks the end of this long section. Sag station 2 comes at mile ~25. After refueling, A right hand turn on to gilberts creek rd will give you a moment to eat your Clif bars and trail mix before you roll into another climb. The next climb is long and steady. For fresh legs this climb is no problem but after 25 mi of grueling Red Bird trails this may prove difficult for manny.  After you reach the summit congratulation this is the last big climb of the day. This ridge trail is a little rougher than the previous sections. Protect your machine from the rock gardens. A puncture this late could derail your race. At ~mile 32 you will each the final SAG station in sugar creek. you will have about 10mi to the finish line. Grab some supplies and get ready for what lies ahead. A slight climb out from sugar creek will have you looking at some nice flowy trail. The Forest service as been working hard on this section fixing ruts and damage. This will be the smoothest section of the day. As you are nearing the end of the crest trail you will begin a steep descent into Peabody and the finish line. This section is rocky steep and rough. Ride within your limits no senses in going OTB at the end of the race. When you reach the bottom of the hill get ready to sprint as the finish line is coming up. Cross the finish line and give yourself a pat on the back. You just finished the hardest MTB race in Ky.         

Course description 40K-

The 40k course will storm out of the Peabody Trail Head onto Hwy 66 then onto Double Creek Rd with the 80k racers. The first major climb comes quick as you climb out of the river bottoms to the ridge. A gravel road will take us to the top of what's called Trace Branch. The summit of this climb is about ~mile 4.5 of the race. You will cross the ridge and descend into a deep valley. This trail can become pretty wet depending on rainfall for the area. This section will have you crossing slick creeks and rocks. it will be very fast as it has a downhill grade for ~4 miles. The first SAG station comes at mile 7. General bike tools water and race snacks, will be available. A short stretch of road will take you to the Crest Trail. The 40k and the 80k course will split here. A left hand turn from the trail will start a steep climb for you. We have named this hill Honey Bun Hill for (once you see it) an obvious reason. If your a strong climber this is your chance to build your lead. As you climb out of the top you will rejoin the 80k course for a nice flow descent into Sag station 2. If you skipped the first station plan to to stop here and refuel. A left hand turn onto gilberts creek road will give you a moment to eat your Clif bars and trail mix before you roll into another climb. The sugar creek road climb will lead you back onto the Crest Trail. with about 5 mi of trail left its time to push hard. The Forest service as been working hard on this section fixing ruts and damage. This will be the smoothest section of the day. As you are nearing the end of the crest trail you will begin a steep descent into Peabody and the finish line. This section is rocky steep and rough. Ride within your limits no senses in going OTB at the end of the race. When you reach the bottom of the hill get ready to sprint as the finish line is coming up. Cross the finish line and give yourself a pat on the back. You just finished the hardest MTB race in Ky. 

Sag Stations and Support

We will be running 3 sag sation with drop bag services. Each station will have water, first aid kits and various race snacks.

EventNotes:
Welcome to the ShredHER DSM MTB skills clinic powered by Kilowatt Coaching! Here's what to expect:

 

WHERE:

JUNE Skills Clinics: June skills clinics will be held at the Rose Garden, 4500 Grand Ave., Des Moines, IA 50312 (go to / google the Ashworth Splash Pad)

AUGUST Skills Clinics: August skills clinics will be held at Rose Garden, 4500 Grand Ave., Des Moines, IA 50312 (go to / google the Ashworth Splash Pad)

SEPTEMBER Skills Clinics: September skills clinics will be held at Rose Garden, 4500 Grand Ave., Des Moines, IA 50312 (go to / google the Ashworth Splash Pad)

 

WHAT:

Beginner Two Hour Clinic:

This clinic will cover the foundational skills for people new to off-road riding and/or new to riding a mountain bike (flat handlebar, vs drop handlebar). 

 

15-min - Intros and Bike ABCs

15-min - Neutral/Ready Position

20-min - Bike/Body Separation - Side/Side & Fore/Aft

15-min - Braking

15-min - Shifting/Ratcheting

15-min - Climbing & Dismounts 

15-min - Descending & Dismounts

10-min - Wrap-up

 

This clinic is right for you if:

  • You are interested in getting off road, but don’t know where to begin.
  • You have not attended a skills clinic previously (or want more practice with these skills).
  • These skills are not familiar terms.
  • You want to connect with more women riding dirt.
  • You like to have fun, laugh, encourage friends, and challenge yourself.

 

Intermediate Two Hour Clinic:

This clinic will cover the foundational skills for people familiar with off-road riding and interested in advancing their MTB handling.

 

15-min - Intros and Bike ABCs

10-min - Neutral/Ready Warm up

10-min - Trackstand

20-min - Cornering

15-min - Wheel Lifts - Front & Rear

15-min - Level Lift

15-min - ¼ Punch Front Wheel Lift

15-min - Roll Down Lunge

05-min - Wrap-up

 

This clinic is right for you if:

  • You regularly ride off-road (Denman/Sycamore) and want to level up your riding.
  • You have attended a Kilowatt Coaching or other BICP based beginner skills clinic.
  • The beginner skills are familiar terms and the intermediate skills are not familiar.

Join us for the 14th anniversary of the Roe Jan Ramble Bike Tour! It's free to all participants and is sponsored by the towns of Copake, Hillsdale and Ancram, NY on the border of Massachusetts. There are 6 routes to choose from (10, 18, 25, 35, 50 miles, and 62.5 miles/100km) on quiet country roads in some of the most beautiful scenery of the Hudson Valley & Taconic foothills you've ever seen.

While the ride is free, we encourage donations to support the Harlem Valley Rail Trail, a publicly accessible trail managed by New York State Parks Department that connects walkers, cyclists and recreationalists from Wassaic to Hillsdale, NY with plans to continue north.

Register to ride right here on Bikereg.com. Once you register, you'll receive a fundraising page to donate or send to friends. If you'd like to contribute now or pledge to a registered rider, go to: https://www.pledgereg.com/roejanramble 

Our ride starts and ends at Copake Memorial Park, 305 Mountain View Road, Copake, NY 12516. The 62.5 mile/100km and 50 mile routes start first at 8:30 AM, the 10 mile route leaves last at 11:00 AM on Saturday, September 19, 2026. On-site parking is free. Check-in starts at 7:30 AM.

Note: You MUST wear a helmet to participate in the Ramble. Pedal assist e-bikes are permitted. Throttle e-bikes are not. Junior registrants (those under 18 years old) must bring a hardcopy of the registration form, signed by a parent or guardian. To print a copy, click here.

Find out more information and updates at our website: https://www.roejanramble.org

EventNotes:
Carpenter Cross - TRIFECTA

Course Map - !BRAND NEW LOCATION! - Please look for the course map on our facebook page as we get closer to the event date!

OUR 3rd NEW VENUE THIS YEAR COMPLETES THE CARPENTER CROSS TRIFECTA

Venue

This year Carpenter Cross will take place in Chestnut Creek Park.  Of course we are staying in Horsham Township, Pennsylvania, which is located close to PA Turnpike "Exit 343 Willow Grove" and only 40 minutes from Philadelphia and Delaware. 

Like us on Facebook and get updated information ... including prizes, sponsors, and a sneak peek at the course ...  https://www.facebook.com/CarpenterCrossCX

Directions

273 Lower State Rd.
HORSHAM, PA 19044

Registration

  • Racing age is determined by your age on December 31, 2027 (not 2026)
  • Please pre-register to avoid paying $10 day-of fee
  • Registration opens @ 7:15 am and closes 15 min. before the start of each race
  • $12 for additional races
  • Mountain bikes without bar ends are ok to race

Licensing Requirements

  • USA Cycling license is required to race (Not for KIDS Race)
  • One-Day licenses will be available at the registration table: Beginner $15 | Experienced $35

Call-up Protocol

  • Order of pre-registration will be called accordingly
  • Riders MUST pre-register to be seeded
  • Staging will begin 10 minutes prior to each race

Staging 

All racers should present to the start grid 15 minutes prior to the start of their race. 

Lapped Riders
Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them.

Technical Pit
A double-sided pit will be marked and available approximately half way through the course. If riders enter the pit, they must make some sort of exchange or mechanical adjustment before re-entering course.

Race Results

Results will be posted after the conclusion of each race at a location designated by the race director and announced at the start line by the chief referee. After results have been posted racers will have a 15 minute protest period to resolve any discrepancies. It is the racers’ responsibility to verify their result during this 15 minute protest period. After the 15 minute protest period results will be final and will not be changed afterwards. Any further disputes must be addressed in writing via email to the riders Local Association contact.

Parking
Use the parking lot in Chestnut Creek Park.  Please park as close as possible to the vehicle next to you without leaving any big gaps. Please DO NOT park in any of the nearby neighborhoods or across the street. 

Clothing Helmets are required for all riders on bicycles, even when not actively racing (eg, while riding from the parking lot). Per USAC regulations, racers must wear a jersey with sleeves covering the shoulders. No tank tops are allowed. Race radios and earphones for playback (eg, mp3 player) are not allowed while racing.

Kids Race A fun kids race will start at 12:15 pm for kids too young to race on the real course (10 and Under).  A parent must sign the event release form prior to the race, and each kid will be given a race number. Pedal bikes or strider bikes are acceptable. All entrants will receive prizes for participation.

Food TBD

Restrooms Park restrooms will be open, as well as a couple extra porta potties located next the restrooms and near the upper corner of the main parking lot.

Race Cancellation Policy: The course is Horsham Township property. If weather conditions are such that the race would cause significant damage to the property, eg, heavy rains and water drenched grounds prior to and during the event, the race may be canceled. The race promoter will make every attempt to determine prior to race day if the race needs to be canceled, however, under extreme conditions the entire race may need to be canceled on the day of the race. Every effort will be made to hold the race, including making course modifications if necessary. If the race is canceled on the day prior to the race, notification will be sent to all pre-registered racers via email, and via the race's Facebook page. If the race is canceled prior to the event date, then registration fees, minus bikereg fees, will be refunded to those racers. 

Other than these specific weather conditions - there are NO REFUNDS!

Support

Thank you to Horsham Township  for making this race happen.  Please do your part when leaving Chestnut Creek Park and take out what you brought in.  All Horsham Township property's are drug and alcohol free so please honor the rules so we can return here next year to race.

AND A HUGE THANK YOU TO OUR SPONSORS!!!

Venue Camping — Reserved Spots Only

Camping at the venue is available in the designated CBMR parking area and is limited to 150 campers. To camp at the venue, each person must reserve a spot by purchasing it with their registration. Spots are first come, first served, so reserve early.

Venue Camping Rules

Due to increased bear activity on the mountain this season and the parking lot surface, all campers must follow these requirements:

  • Camping is permitted only in the designated camping area
  • Tents must be properly secured. If tents cannot be staked into the lot surface, weight them down well. If you use rocks from around the parking lot, return them to where you found them before leaving
  • Absolutely no food or scented items (even deodorant) may be stored in tents — this is a hard rule due to bear activity
  • If you're traveling in an SUV, wagon, truck, or similar vehicle, we strongly encourage sleeping in your vehicle as the safer option
  • No water, sewer, or power hookups are available; all vehicles must be self-contained
  • There will be portable toilets and bear proof trash containers for your use in the camping area.
  • No alcohol is permitted in the lot
  • Dogs must remain on a leash at all times
  • NO FIRES
  • Keep the camping area clean; all trash must go in the provided containers
  • All local, state, and federal laws apply
  • Highly suggest having bear spray. They do not respond to air horns.
  • A Camp Host will be on premises all weekend to answer any questions.

FREE Camping Options

Free camping is available in local camping areas and on the Western Colorado University campus. If you would like to camp on the Western campus, contact race director Jason Tullous (jtullous@western.edu) for information.

Join the Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia for Roll Wit It, a Gran Fondo-style Fun Ride and Challenge benefitting the Bicycle Coalition Youth Cycling (BCYC) program. This high-impact program prepares youth ages 12-18 for success on and off the bike, supporting them as they develop healthy habits, leadership, and independence through the sport of cycling. 

When you ride Roll Wit It, you’re paying it forward — your entry fee and team fundraising goes to support the BCYC collegiate scholarship program.

About the 2026 Routes: 

  • The Whiz — a 17 mile casual loop featuring a trip through Manayunk's Main Street and one hill before the rest stop in the middle. (https://www.strava.com/routes/3509647406284203612)

  • The Works — a scenic 69.8 mile route with a few signature climbs, plus a segment of the Chester Country Trail and a dip into Valley Forge National Historic Park. Our rest & refuel partner sites will be located in Narberth, Bryn Mawr, Wayne, Phoenixville, Valley Forge park, and Conshohocken. (https://www.strava.com/routes/3504298350867027966)

A ride through the wilds of northern Franklin County from 8am to 3pm starting at the Choiniere Farm Trails. This is a fundraising event for the Franklin County Trails Alliance. We’ve teamed up with the Choiniere Farm to help you connect with the land, the watershed, and the amazing trails in this region! 
About the Organization
The Franklin County Trails Alliance promotes responsible trail use, conducts trail maintenance, and advocates for the development and accessibility of local non-motorized, off-road recreational trails. Learn more about their work at www.fctavt.com
 
The Details 
Your registration will include lunch, fantastic rest stop treats, and socks for $70. Registration on the day of the ride increases to $100. There will be two loops, 17 and 43 miles, beginning at the Choiniere Family Farm trails in Highgate, traveling along the border with Canada, by Lake Carmi, and on a section of the Lamiolle Valley Rail Trail. Register now by clicking the register button! 
Sunday Rides 
Highgate, Vermont sits on the Lamoille Valley Rail Trail (LVRT), a 93-mile trail connecting the town of Swanton, Vt. to St. Johnsbury, Vt. The Missisquoi Valley Rail Trail, a 26-mile trail connecting the town of St. Albans to Richford, intersects the LVRT just six miles from Highgate. Consider coming for the Franklin Forty on Saturday and staying in the area to ride one of the rail trails on Sunday. 
Where does the money go? 
Franklin County Trails Alliance is working with several partners and municipalities to build a new multi-use, 8-mile-long connected ridgeline trail between the St. Albans Town Forest and the Missisquoi Valley Rail Trail, linking trails between Hard’ack Recreation Area & Trails, St. Albans downtown, and Swanton. This project starts in 2025 and will be looking to complete in 2025/26. Cost estimates range from $150,000 to $200,000!

Please respect all practice schedule times as our Athletic Training staff can better support us during these time frames. 

XC practice - the course will be open and available to ride on Friday by 11 AM until 5:30 PM, and then again on Saturday morning prior to the start of racing at 8:15 AM. Please respect these practice time windows as they will ensure the course is well marked and safe.

STXC practice - the course will be open by 7:30 AM on Sunday morning up until the team relay at 8:15 AM. Portions can be ridden on Friday and Saturday, but it overlaps our Dual Slalom course, so priority goes to DS until Sunday morning.

Riders should be ready for call ups at least 10 minutes prior to their race start.

Podiums immediately after near finish line.

STXC - course will last approximately 3 to 3.5 minutes. Start line will be separate from the finish line. We will be pulling riders in the STXC! Podiums immediately after near finish line.

Downhill - One run only. There will be NO PARKING at the shuttle pick up or drop off anywhere on the gravel road during DH shuttles or racing. All cars must be parked at the gym parking lot! Full face helmets are mandatory for practice and racing. Podiums at the gym for those not in a hurry to get home!

You must present your ID and a copy of each rider’s photo ID and a statement of permission. A text or email containing a photo of a rider’s ID and their statement will work.

Registration will also be available on Saturday and Sunday.

 

Course Description 

After starting in historic downtown Frederick Maryland, the 87 mile Gran Fondo National Series, Gran Route, will gain over 10,000 feet of elevation through several different state parks, municipal forests, protected watersheds, and the Catoctin Mountain National Park.  Riders will travel northwest out of the city of Frederick before entering the Frederick Municipal Forest where the first timed section will gain over 1270 feet in a 5.6 mile race segment. At the top riders will be able to relax and enjoy the cool mountain forest as the course plummets over the west side of the mountain range.

The second timed section ascends the southern approach to Harp Hill for a punchy up-down-up-down-up lasting for a brief 1.4 miles and 279 feet of vertical gain. For the next 25 miles and 2500 feet of cumulative gain, the route then follows a mix of small and obscure backroads heading north towards the decommissioned military base of Fort Ritchie.

Time Section #3 is a more dynamic segment and certainly cannot be called a timed climb. Section #3 will require riders to use caution and technical skill with several 90° turns including an old bridge crossing and tarp & chip road surface. The section starts on a wide downhill roadway where for the first 4.9 miles riders lose 500 feet of elevation before hitting the last 1k and 300 vertical feet to the finish of section #3 on top of Hornets Nest Road. Time segment #3 known as The Gully of Darius is a total of 5.5 miles -574 /+386 feet.  From here the route heads south and works its way back exploring nooks and crannies in the Catoctin Mountain Range and travels through Catoctin Mountain National Park  for 22 miles and +2250 feet of untimed pedaling. Past riders will be able to take special appreciation as they descend Park Central Road, which was used in the opposite direct as race section #2 in past years.

As Gran Route riders approach mile 71 they need to take in a deep breath, shake out their legs and prepare for the hardest segment of the day, (this segment also counts as a time segment for Medio Route riders). Section #4 is 11.4 miles +1203 feet and will test every rider’s ability! The segment starts by gaining 784 feet over the first 4.6 miles and then continues for a challenging and undulating 6.8 miles on top of the mountain ridge on Gambrill Park Road through Frederick Watershed and into Gambrill State Park. After completing time section #4, riders will have over 1000 feet of elevation on their side as they drop off the mountain range and into the valley towards the finish, but completing the route in not over, there are still some hills that are sure to make riders know they are still alive. Riders will return back into historic downtown Fredrick and be welcome to well deserved festivities at the finish line, complete with great food, beverage, and more fun.

Are you a cycling enthusiast looking for an exciting opportunity to be a part of a national series event? We are seeking volunteers to help us with the upcoming Gran Fondo National Series! Check out the volunteering opportunities below! This is a unique chance to be a part of a prestigious event, meet new people, and contribute to the success of one of the country's largest cycling events series! We have a variety of time slots available, so whether you have a few hours or a full day to spare, we can accommodate your schedule. Aid station - Help hand out food and water to tired and hungry cyclists. 
Event Break down - After the awards ceremony we start breaking down the event expo.

EventNotes:
Experience Southwest Michigan’s Premier Fall Ride!

Join us on Sunday, September 20, 2026, for Bike Friendly Kalamazoo’s 8th Annual Fall Bike Celebration. Starting and finishing at the historic Vicksburg Historic Village, this event offers expertly designed routes through serene countryside, historic landmarks, and scenic waterways—plus full support and a post-ride feast!

Highlights & Route Options:

  • Shipshewana Century (100 Miles): Our signature "two states of mind" route starts in Vicksburg, MI, and winds into the heart of Indiana's charming Amish countryside.
  • Covered Bridge Routes (3 Options): Cross the St. Joseph River on Michigan’s longest, most photogenic covered wooden bridge.
  • Gravel & Mixed Surface (2 Options): Take the path less traveled through the hauntingly beautiful Rawson's King Mill Park along Nottawa Creek.
  • Family & Casual Rides: Relaxed routes utilizing paved multi-use trails, perfect for riders of all ages and skill levels.
  • Historic Charm: All routes showcase Vicksburg Quilt Trail murals and end on the grounds of the lovingly curated Vicksburg Historic Village.

What’s Included:

  • Fully marked, scenic routes with downloadable GPS maps
  • Well-stocked SAG fuel stops & dedicated vehicle support
  • Delicious post-ride meal included with your registration!

Choose your distance and register today to lock in your spot for the best fall riding experience in Southwest Michigan!

PERKS OF PRE-REGISTERING ONLINE

Lock in your registration early to score these exclusive extras:

  • Free Ice Cream: Enjoy ice cream at Apple Knocker’s Ice Cream Parlor (coupon valid through the end of September!).
  • 10% Off Craft Beer: Get a 10% discount coupon for your bill at The Distant Whistle Brewhouse (also valid through the end of September).
  • Skip the Sunday Line! Pick up your packet/wristband at Saturday’s Ice Cream Social to skip the Day-Of Registration desk entirely on Sunday morning and roll straight to the start line.

Detailed Event Guide & Route Info For full details on Start Times & Locations, downloadable GPS Routes, Parking, SAG Stop schedules, SWAG, and Saturday's Ice Cream Social, visit our Official Fall Bike Celebration Bike Tour Page for the most up-to-date info.

ROUTES

GRAVEL ROUTES - 32 & 59 miles

START & FINISH LOCATION

All of our routes provide a wonderful way to enjoy the beauty of the fall on the calm rural roads in scenic SW Michigan.  All will get glimpses of the Vicksburg Quilt Trail paintings and start/finish at the fascinating Vicksburg Historic Village.

Families must complete a form that lists all participating family members. Family registration is limited to family members living at the same address.

Fees are non-refundable unless BFK cancels the Ride, otherwise, Ride is rain or shine; route cancellations may occur due to road closures, emergencies, extreme weather, public health considerations and other unforeseen and unavoidable causes with little or no prior notice.  Registrations are not transferrable.  This overview may not reflect last minute changes; please refer to our Fall Bike Celebration website for more detail about the routes and features.  We like transparency!  BikeReg charges a nominal non-refundable fee for their handling; T-Shirts are taxable; we've been told nothing else is taxed.  You can register through BikeReg knowing that they are handling the security of their credit card transactions.

Have a safe and happy ride!

It’s Supposed To Be Hard

You're not seeing things.  We give you more for riding 50 miles on a true New England course than most races give you for winning.  Why?  Because this race is hard, that's why.  Oh, and the prizes are insane if you should so happen to do well at this thing.  What better way to finish off the local marathon racing season?

Field Limits and Registration

The field limit is 250 racers total.  We could fit more but we don't want to, so deal with it.  We also do not have the staff or the patience to deal with day-of registrations this year, so plan for that.

Why Register Early

As a proud sponsor of the BikeWorks SVC Dirt Cup, 24 Auto Group is providing FREE Freetown 50 t-shirts to the first 150 riders who register! 

Courses

This loop is what we've landed on over the years as being the most balanced and most fun, which means 50 milers get 2 laps, which also means more stops at Feed Zones and better accountability for us.  It means hitting the same technical sections 2 times, but also it means hitting the nice fire road sections 2 times.  Know you'll enjoy it because the first year we did it was our biggest and most well reviewed.  Not like you have a choice!

This course makes it possible to have a 25 mile which we're stoked about.  You deserve the full course at least once.

The 43 mile and metric century routes  provide a picturesque ride through Lehigh Twp and Moore Twp in Northampton County with 2 challenging hill climbs and a passage through a covered bridge in Carbon County.  The 19 mile ride stays on the south side of the Blue Mtn range and includes smaller climbs to accommodate the intermediate and beginner cyclists and is equally picturesque riding through farm country.  The metric ride combines both rides for a more challenging route for experienced cyclists.

Detailed event notes for Valley Preferred Cycling Center (VPCC) Try the Track programs and activities can be found here on our website.

Registering for a Community Program at the VPCC for 2026 can include the option of purchasing USA Cycling Membership + Race License. The Membership + Race license benefit is that riders can later compete in competitive events, receive secondary medical insurance, and have the option to purchase on-bike injury coverage with a $0 deductible. Here is the member benefits page.  Again, this is optional and not needed to register.

If you would like to utilize these benefits for your Try the Track session, please follow the following process to sign up. 

*If you already have an active USA Cycling Membership +Race License, you can proceed to Step 2, register for your selected Try the Track date. 

Step 1 — Obtain Your USA Cycling Membership + Race License Number (Optional)

Proceed to the USAC get started web page. Scroll down to the bottom and click on join now to get started.

  • USA Cycling recently adjusted the membership price from $20 to $40. A discount code is available that reduces the membership fee back to $20, regardless of whether auto-renew is selected. This code works for both new and renewing members.  That code is USAC-TW20X.
  • During checkout, riders must open the Discount box near the end of the process to apply the code.
  • The +Race License is free for juniors and free for first-time USA Cycling members for the first year.
  • New members receive a free one-year annual race license, but they must manually add the license to their USA Cycling account.
  • Returning members should review the current USA Cycling fee schedule:

If you have a question or need a refund, you must contact USA Cycling Membership directly.

Step 2 — Register on BikeReg

This is an old school, classic single loop backcountry race. The namesake  is from an on course incident with a rattlesnake many years ago. You have to be tough for this 24 mile back country loop in the heart of Dankness that characterizes Canaan. This is a fundraiser for Blackwater Bicycle Association.  

The race  starts in Davis on River Road Trail to Yellow Birch and then climbs up a virtual creek bed, The Davis Trail (Allegheny Trail) to Plantation Trail . You'll make a right onto Plantation Trail and then a left onto Fire Trail #6 Trail.   Make a left onto Canaan Loop Road  (Forest Road 13) and enjoy several miles on the gravel. There will be an aid station on the gravel road at Davis Trail, so you can refuel on the easy road before you get to Fire Trail 3.   Descend Fire Trail 3 to Plantation.  Take a left onto Plantation back to Davis Trail (Allegheny Trail). Make a right on Davis to descend what you climbed earlier to Blackwater Falls State Park and do Yellow Birch(again) and the River Road Trail back into Davis. Last year that was a full aid station, but his year will just be water.   If you are a DUO Team, this is where you will tag your partner for the next leg.  Leaving town,  you'll tackle the rock tech of Splashdam Trail and will start to feel the hard, slow miles. At the Judge Pearson Bridge, there will be a FULL AID STATION.  It's a perfect spot to refuel because, there is no rest for the weary as you then climb Hoodoo and descend the Moon Rocks searching for that sweet locals line. Hammer back on Trials Trail. Wet lube and extra chamois cream are recommended! Registration opens at 8:30 at Davis City Park Pavilion. Racers meeting is at 9:45 at Start line. The Start of the race is at 10am at the beginning of the River Road Trail(South side of Rt 32 Bridge) .  New this year, the FINISH is at the Davis Riverwalk Park. Please pre ride the start and finish.  Post race meal by the fabulous SIRIANNI'S Pizza and FREE t-shirt are included in the race entry at the DAVIS CITY PARK

ROR 2026   SAME COURSE as 2025

The DUO class is a just for fun class.  There will be no prizes issued for that class, but you will be officially timed and have placing for that class.  The reasoning behind that is E bikes are allowed on the second half of the race course.

This race is made possible through permission of  the land owners.  We would like to thank the West Virginia Land Trust for use of the trails on the Yellow Creek Natural Area that includes the Moon Rocks and Hoodoo Rocks. We thank National Youth Science Academy for use of their land. We thank the U.S. Forest Service for the permit to use Plantation, Fire Trail 6, and Davis Trail and Fire Trail 3.  We also want to thank the West Virginia DNR for use of their trails in Blackwater Falls and Little Canaan Wildlife Management Area.  Big thank you to the private property owners that have generously allowed us use of their land for the race:  The Snarrs, Western Pocahontas Properties Limited, and CPG Development.  Thank you to the Town of Davis. We also want to thank Blackwater Bikes for helping with the race and all the amazing volunteers who helped with trail work and putting on the race.

PLEASE BE AT REGISTRATION AT 8:30am at Davis City Park (please park there as well) to sign waiver, pick up your race tag and pick up your free t-shirt.  There is a Bathroom at the Riverfront Park .

PARKING :  please park at the Davis Riverfront Park across from the Shop N Save.

‘CROSS IS BACK IN NEW HAVEN!! For the third year running, New Haven Bicycling Club and True Cyclery are bringing back the barnstorming good time that is HIDDEN VALLEY CX! We learned a ton last year and listened to your valuable feedback. So this year we've made some changes: we’ve expanded the course, we've moved the starting line, added a beginners' race, and perhaps most importantly, secured an extra portapotty. And we got a sink. (Well, we booked those things, hopefully they get delivered). What are we keeping? The same good vibes, clean racing, and downright fun of our inaugural event! 

This year's 'cross is happening at Forbes Bluff, a secret meadow (a Hidden Valley, perhaps??), in between Fort Hale Park and the Pardee Seawall. It seems like the Big G just dropped this purpose built cyclocross course out of the heavens and right into the easternmost slice of New Haven. We can't wait to throw some tape up, carve it up, and rut it out! We're got lots of grass, a minimal amount of trails, loads of elevation changes, and a choose-your-own-adventure ride/run-up! 

BIB PICKUP/REGISTRATION!

Registration will be in the big pavilion and will open at 7:30 am. For anyone not already registered, day of registration will be available for $55, unless you're jumping in a second race for the day, then that is $20. Let us know at the table and we'll give you the discount code. 

PARKING!

There is very limited parking available at the venue on Woodward Ave. Most of this will be coned off for volunteers and officials, but we will also have a drop off spot marked. THIS IS A RESIDENTIAL AREA AND IT IS YOUR RESPONSIBILITY TO READ ALL PARKING SIGNS AND TO MAKE SURE THAT YOU DO NOT BLOCK ANY DRIVEWAYS OR HYDRANTS! There are a few designated handicap parking spots on Woodward, do not park in them if you're not legally entitled to.

  • Yellow lines on the map indicate street parking and parking lots: PLEASE CHECK SIGNAGE AND DO NOT BLOCK DRIVEWAYS, HANDICAP SPACES, OR HYDRANTS! The south side of Woodward is available next to the venue and both the east and west sides open as you go further north. Pope St and Morse Pl have available parking on both sides of the street but Fort Hale Rd only allows parking on the north side. Available lots include Fort Hale Park just north of us (with a small playground for kiddos) and further out East Shore Park has 3 lots, all about 0.5-0.8 miles away. Kinda far, but hey! Free warmup! There is also a large playground there for kiddos. East Shore Park is also a great place to get a grassy warmup in if you're not able to get on the course. PLEASE DO NOT RIDE ON ANY OF THE ATHLETIC FIELDS!
  • Red boxes indicate Absolutely No Parking! The race takes place next to an active military/Coast Guard station. Don't even think about it. The other red boxes are privately owned property that we do not have access to. Don't risk getting towed!
  • Blue lines outline the course and the thicker part show where the volunteer parking/drop off zone will be. The blue R indicates registration at the pavilion. 

THE COURSE!

You can expect lots of sharp turns, hairpin cornering, and a few bellowing straightaways. There's one long stair set that can be ridden along the side or you can run it (we're calling it “THE ASCENT” but we forgot to mark it on the map, it's right after the pits through the trees until it opens up again). There's one short run-up in THE BATTLESWAMP. Don't get distracted by the stunning “ocean” views of the Long Island Sound while you're down there, or for that matter as you traverse THE BOARDWALK. There's a fast descent with a lead up of two short sets of wide stairs that can either be ridden or ridden alongside. This leads down to THE GAUNTLET before heading back up via what is quite easily the shortest, straightest stretch of single track on the PMCX calendar. Get back on the three-way straight and then get ready for some uphill chicaning following THE SPEEDWAY. Finally, you'll hit THE NAMELESS DESCENT (also forgot to mark), which drops you back into THE PARTY ZONE. Hit some barriers, swoop past the pits and then cross the finish line with your arms raised whether you've won or not! I mean, well, don't do that if there are more laps left. 

ONE IMPORTANT NOTE! We got some pretty rough storms in the last few weeks and THE NAMELESS DESCENT has seen a bit of washout, so it's GNARLIER THAN PREVIOUS YEARS! Please pre-ride the course and check this spot out as it is different!

Below is the 2025 map, which we expect to be extremely similar to this year's cross, but expect some fine tuning and possible corner-swaps while we're taping up on Saturday, but the general character will remain the same. Here's a preview video of 2024's lap: https://youtu.be/lIqYon9aazI

We are optimistic that the course will be open by 7:30 AM. We have buffered what we hope is an adequate of time in between races for pre-ride. DO NOT GET ON THE COURSE DURING AN ACTIVE RACE! The officials will open up the course, most likely during the final lap of each given race, but IT IS WILDLY IMPORTANT THAT YOU DO NOT PASS AN ACTIVE RACER DURING YOUR PRERIDE OR YOU WILL BE SUBJECT TO DISQUALIFICATION! The course will be modified during the kiddo race, but 90% of it will be available for pre-ride while they're out there. DO NOT RIDE ON THE KIDDO COURSE UNLESS YOU ARE A KIDDO IN THAT RACE!

That's it! If you have any questions, reach out to us at info@newhavenbicyclingclub.org

EventNotes:
REGISTRATION ENDS @ 5pm on September 19 or when we're sold out.

THERE WILL BE NO RACE DAY REGISTRATION

CAMPING AVAILABLE

AMAZING LODGE ROOMS AND CABINS AVAILABLE IN THE PARK!!

 

Welcome to registration for the seventh Annual Cacapon Enduro

PLEASE NOTE: The park has asked us to avoid using the gravel road to the top as a climb, use designated climb trails for each stage. Riding up the road can lead to a DQ.

The hub of the race will, again, be the Batt Picnic Area at Cacapon Resort State Park. The signs are pretty clear and we will supplement with event signs. This is a "chip and go" race, so arrive to the Batt Picnic Shelter between 8am and 10am to pick up your chip. After getting your timing chip, you can begin riding up the new climbing trail to the top, Boy Scout. There will be a fee for lost timing chips. Your chip number is noted in your registration information so please return your chip to registration after you finish your race or there will be a charge.

Race Cutoff is 3:00PM and will be strictly enforced.... cross the line at 3:01 and results will not be counted.

PRIZE: For OPEN Class- there will be nice cash prizes for the top 3 finishes. For all other classes, will have bragging rights and swag from the prize table!

Stages are NOW SET! We are in the process of building 35 miles of new trail, with funding from this race going directly to support new trails! This year most people will race 5 stages in 17 miles with 2,225' of climbing. Pros get an additional stage, so their total will be 23 miles with 3,519' of climbing!!! 

For a link to the racecourse that you can use race day and for practice, visit:

2026 Cacapon Enduro | WV Enduro Series Mountain Biking Route | Trailforks

https://www.mtbproject.com/trail/7076830/2026-cacapon-enduro-route-5-stages-for-all-except-pro-expert

 

WEEKEND AGENDA

ALL STAGES WILL BE MARKED BY 6PM FRIDAY.

Friday, September 18 Camping Opens 9am. Pre rides on trails all day. You can shuttle to the top, gate will be unlocked. 

Saturday, September 29 Pre ride. You can shuttle to the top of the mountain, gate will be unlocked. 

Sunday, September 20 RACE DAY

     - 7:00 Begin parking / shuttling to Batt Picnic Shelter. We have limited parking available at the Batt Shelter, so carpool when able. Suggest campers either ride up or shuttle together when able.

     - 8:00am-10:00am Pick up timing chips at Batt Picnic Shelter. Cut off at 10am, no late check in allowed

     - 8am-10:00am Begin race with ride up Boy Scout 

     - 3:00pm All racers must be finished. Any chips with times after 3:30pm will be DQ

     - 4:00pm Awards at Batt Picnic Shelter

The park features many cabins and a newly updated lodge with restaurant. Here is a link to lodging reservations.  

https://wvstateparks.com/park/cacapon-resort-state-park/

The park does not have a campground BUT the park superintendent loves mountain bikers and is setting up a dedicated camping area again this year. This year the campground area will be at the swimming lake parking lot and will be open Friday, September 18 to Sunday September 20.  Early set up will be allowed the evening of Thursday, September 17. This camping area is a paved and gravel parking lot suitable for car camping and tent camping. This area can also handle pull behind campers and RV's as well, BUT there is no hook up and NO dump station. Camping will be only $50 for the whole weekend and is first come, first served with sites. We do need an estimate of the number of campers, so please note if camping for the event. Registration for camping will be at the Lodge Front Desk. Just tell them you are there for the Enduro race. The beach bath house will be open for the campers, so HOT showers will be available.

For those unfamiliar with the area, Cacapon State Park is located on US Route 522 at the Virginia-West Virginia state line. It is 30 minutes north of Winchester, Va., 15 minutes south of Berkeley Springs, WV, and 20 minutes west of Martinsburg, WV. This is an easy drive from the DMV, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, and everywhere in Va and WV. 

Like what you are seeing us do at Cacapon? If so, please donate through the non-profit Foundation so we can continue to develop the trail system. The park has dedicated nearly 1,000 acres to mountain biking and we are about to kick the build into high gear! We will debut the new skills park this year for everyone to enjoy with much more to come! Every dollar helps! Here's the link to make a donation: https://www.crspf.org/mountain-biking/

Here is a link to the whole course on MtbProject. It is suggested that you download the app and use this race day for navigation.

https://www.mtbproject.com/trail/7076830/2026-cacapon-enduro-route-5-stages-for-all-except-pro-expert
 

All of the hubs on the mountain now have letter designations. They also have a QR code to the Cacapon map on MtbProject. 3 Stages start at HUB K near the overlook and across from Upper Thunderstruck: Stage 1 Rocket, Stage 2 Livin' on the Edge, and Stage E (eBikes only) Rock Star.

STAGES CAN BE RACED IN ANY ORDER


STAGE 1: Rocket (New trail on back side of mountain). Starts at HUB K, near the overlook. It starts pedaly, but picks up steam and flows through 4 good rock gardens. At the first intersection, turn LEFT for a short section on Misty Mountain for a ripping-fast addition to Rocket. After a sharp (a 270 degree flattish turn) look for the yellow ribbons and arrows and transfer first up the old logging road, cross the hub you came through (careful crossing active race trail!) and proceed up Misty Mountain to Porcupine. Turn right on Porcupine to the Jeep road, and go back up to the overlook.

STAGE 2: Livin' on the Edge (New trail) This is a fast, flowing descent that will test your bike control on flat turns. Then the transfer is a short, but punchy climb continuing on the trail back to the top of Giddy Up.

STAGE 3: You'll race the FULL Giddy-Up! This is a 2.6 mile trail that descends 832 feet back to Batt. THIS IS THE LAST STAGE FOR BEGINNERS. Transition after this is back up Boy Scout.

STAGE 4: Shakedown. (BEGINNERS SKIP THIS STAGE) Part of the old Giddy Up from races in the past. The name says it all. It is loose and fast with a couple of drops that will be required, or you'll have to navigate a chicane to slow you down. Transfer back up Boy Scout (lower and middle) and then carefully cross Giddy Up and get on Girl Scout. The race will start before the big boulder on the left on Girl Scout and flow into Middle Thunderstruck

STAGE 5: End of Girl Scout to Middle and Lower Thunderstruck. (BEGINNERS SKIP THIS STAGE) What a way to finish. Fast, rocky, and loose. Brings you back to the Batt parking lot.

The race is 17.9 miles long and has 2,325' of climbing... except for Pro and Expert...

STAGE 6 PRO and EXPERT ONLY: Ziler Loop South. This is a classic. Rocky, rutted, loose, and rowdy. There are a couple of punchy climbs in the middle. Transfer to stage 3 by climbing back to the overlook for a second trip up the mountain.

Full pro race is 24.5 miles and has 3,466feet of climbing!


Stage 7E eBikes only: ***we will make a call on this stage Saturday, the software may not support this as a separate stage*** eBikes Only: This stage is on RockStar and starts at Hub K, same as Stages 1 & 2. This is the rockiest trail in the park, and probably rockiest trail on the east coast! 2.4 miles long and climb 99' and then descend 566'. Rock Star ends at Misty Mountain. Ride that back to the same transfer trail as stage 1.
For eBike Sport, race is 23.3 miles and has 2,891' of climbing

For eBike Pro, that extends to 29.9 miles and 4,032' of climbing!

 

PLEASE NOTE: The park has asked that we use trails for transfers only, no riding on the gravel road to the top, even for e-Bikes. Stick to the trails for climbing. Also, there will be NO SHUTTLES. Anyone caught shuttling or riding up the road faces a DQ and eternal shame, humiliation and embarrassment!

EventNotes:
Another year, another ride.  Are you ready?  The Cannonball is back —and better than ever.  Saddle up for scenic routes, stocked stops and smooth spins through Virginia’s backcountry.  Crush your course of choice and recharge at comfortable rest stops and a well earned post ride meal.  Whether you’re a seasoned cyclist or a weekend warrior, it is your ride, your vibe, your Cannonball.

Our Charitable sponsors this year will be local charities as well as the

YMCA Bright Beginnings Children's program

YMCA Bright Beginnings is a community outreach program that provides children in need with new clothes and school supplies to start the school year with confidence and excitement. The Y organizes planned shopping days and volunteers to shop one-on-one with a child.

WHAT DOES MY REGISTRATION COVER ?

Event insurance, club expenses, permits, post-ride lunch, rest stop food & drinks, advertising and logistics. Oh and of course some really sweet swag!

Additional proceeds will benefit local charities including the YMCA Bright Beginnings program that provides school clothes and supplies for children in need. 

THE ROUTES AND NAVIGATION

The event will feature three course options: a 35.7 mile (Half Metric), a 63 mile (Metric) and a full 100 mile (Century), all winding through some of the most scenic and peaceful roads in Spotsylvania and Caroline Counties.

RideWithGPS (RWGPS) will be available to all participants who have a free RWGPS account or better.  Please be sure to update your downloaded routes on your device the night before the ride in case last minute changes have occurred!

Route markings: PLEASE NOTE: ROADS WILL NOT BE PAINTED. Signage will be posted on hazards, important turns and near rest stops.

Please Download or print a queue sheet for your registered route using the links below (coming soon!). Routes are subject to change, final routes will be posted (Sept 1st) 3 weeks prior to the event and also will be included in a final event email distribution.

35.7 Route

63 Mile Route

100 Cannonball Century Route

STOPS/TREATS/RIDE SUPPORT

Well-stocked rest stops will be available along the routes, each offering essential supplies, a unique treat special to each stop, and a warm, helpful team of volunteers.  Our SAG (Support and Gear) team will be monitoring the routes for your safety.

Afterwards, enjoy a post-ride meal at The YMCA

Pre-registration only. Registration closes Thursday, September 24th at 5pm. Number pickup will be located near the bike shop in the upper lot. When you arrive, send your entire team to the bike shop where they can sign waivers.

ALL RIDERS must sign a RRC liability waiver. There will be iPads set up near registration to easily get this done. Teams will need to have all registered riders sign the waiver before receiving race plates and shuttle wristbands. Doing this on site is the easiest way for the park to ensure all have signed.

The Ride Rock Creek bike park will be open normal hours on Friday. You must purchase a pass in order to ride outside of the designated practice/race hours. The XCO, XCC and slalom courses will not be open for pre-riding Friday. However, the DH race track (Easy A) will be open.

Every team will receive one free shuttle wristband for coaches wishing to be at the top of the downhill run without a bike. Coaches wishing to ride the downhill track can purchase a wristband on the event registration page. Coach ride passes are only available on our registration site. If you wish to purchase these on site, they will only be available at the normal park pricing.

Team and trailer parking will be in the lower pasture parking area. There will be volunteers at the entrance to direct traffic. Trailers can be dropped Friday afternoon or evening to leave for the weekend. Ride Rock Creek, Brevard College and Warren-Wilson College are not responsible for equipment left overnight.

There are two required practice runs for the downhill races. A volunteer will be in the start gate throughout the open practice time placing stickers on number plates to verify these runs have been done. Full face helmets are required for all practice and race runs for downhill and dual slalom. 

Results will be posted on site and on the Webscorer website following the completion of each race. Podium times are listed within the schedule.

All races will use new number plates for chip timing so we will not be using the conference numbers.

EventName: Fifth Annual Tariffville Mountain BIke Extravaganza!
EventNotes:
Come join us for the Tariffville Mountain Bike Extravaganza as part of this year's Tariffville Fall Gathering. Some say that Tariffville is the mountain biking capital of Connecticut (and maybe the universe), so we're putting on this event to prove it. 

Perhaps you've ridden Cowles Park or Penwood, but I'm sure there are lots of secret tunnels, cut throughs and hidden features that you're unaware of. And, if you know them, you know what mega fun trails await. We'll have beginner, intermediate and advanced rides, which should be intuitive in terms of their difficulty. On the MTB rides, someone will be leading and someone will be sweeping, so no need for advance-posted routes or maps. You're also welcome to do your own thing if you want to custom-tailor your ride. 

The rides are free, but we ask that you register so that we know how to distribute volunteers, etc.

I will work with nearby restaurants to try and get food and drink deals as in years past, so you can hang out afterwards without a rumbling stomach.

Direct any questions to Brendan Mahoney-- oiseaux@gmail.com or 860-729-9603. Let me know if you'd like to volunteer!

 

In the event that the bigger event is canceled due to bad weather, the Mountain Bike Extravaganza will also be canceled.

Farm event rules:

1. NO DOGS – Big, little, pure, mutt we love them all, but the only dogs allowed are the family farm dogs. THIS INCLUDES EVERYONE, NOT JUST CAMPERS. 

2. No open fires. You can bring your portable grills or campfire rings but no open campfires.

Please thank the Oesterlings for their hospitality whenever you have the chance.

The only place you will be allowed to drop the food wrappers is at the start/finish line/feed zone area where they must be picked up by a teammate or your support person. DO NOT LITTER or leave your unwanted trash or debris behind.

9. Pack out what you pack in. Going along really well with #9 above. Bring a big ol’ trash bag, put your garbage in your big ol’ trash bag, put your big ol’ trash bag in your car, put your car in your driveway, and put your trash in your trashcan at home. Thanks for helping us keep the place clean. Helping us with little things like this keeps the event going because it keeps my crew, my folks, my outlaws, and my wife happy!

10. We reserve the right to create and impose further rules or do whatever else we want!
