EventNotes:
Cider Cross / Fon Solo Weekend 2026! 

Year Five — Bigger, Better, and More Fun Than Ever!
[October 3-4| Alna, ME]

Forget the pumpkin spice — we’ve got a sour batch of apples ready to be mashed!

Join us for a two-day festival of fall mayhem featuring short-track MTB & CX racing, last-person-standing style trail running, epic gravel rides, and camping under the stars. Whether you're racing, riding, running, or just hanging out by the fire, Cider Cross / Fon Solo has something for everyone.

SATURDAY: CIDER CROSS + BACKYARD ULTRA-STYLE RUN

Cider Cross Race:

  • One 40-minute race with CX and MTB categories
  • About a 1-mile course – re-routed for 2025 to feature faster, more open gravel-friendly sections
  • Expect slop, speed, and heckling
  • Bring any bike — gravel, mountain, cyclocross — whatever rolls!
  • Yes, the optional fire jump is back.
  • Yes, there will be prizes (top 3 per category, TBD)

Last-Person-Standing Trail Run:

  • Race format an easier version of the Backyard Ultra
  • ~1 mile loops on the same course
  • Time limit decreases by 1 minute per lap
    (e.g., Lap 1 = 20 min, Lap 2 = 19 min, etc.)
  • Run till you can't make the cutoff!
  • You can expect 7–8 laps if you're at a 12-min/mile pace
  • Last year, the fastest runners made it down to the 6-minute mark!

Food, drinks, and camping available.

BYOBreakfast! (But seriously, sign up for a camping spot early.)

SUNDAY: THE FON SOLO GRAVEL LOOP

Our grand finale — a gravel adventure through the Sheepscot Valley. This year, we’ve got two route options:

  • Short Loop: ~25 miles — easier & faster than the original loop. Fewer climbs, smoother ride, great for the gravel curious.
  • Full Loop: ~49 miles — the classic, with climbs, views, and chunky gravel madness.  The route will be very similar to last year but we are always looking for areas of improvement!
  • Less full Loop ~41 miles.  The same as the full loop with the furthest 8 miles trimmed off. 

Both routes:

  • Cruise scenic roads and remote stretches of backcountry beauty
  • Roll through the tasting deck at Oxbow Brewing near the finish (yes, seriously)
  • End with good vibes, sore legs, and cold cider

REGISTRATION INFO:

Prepare for an unforgettable cycling adventure in the heart of the Midwest. Whether you're a seasoned gravel racer or a casual rider seeking scenic thrills, our event promises an exhilarating experience for all.

The Old Fashioned Gravel ride/race is back for 2026! We are fortunate enough to have some of the best gravel riding in the Midwest and have put together four routes to show off the local terrain. As with all of our rides, we offer a little bit of everything and welcome EVERYONE from novice riders to the most seasoned racers. The focus of the ride is to bring like-minded individuals together for a great ride, but we will have professional timing so if you want to race we will have you covered too! Routes that will satisfy all of your gravely desires, and a post-ride gathering with food, drink, and hangs with new friends. EventName: Gorey Hollows VIII: The Hollow Heart
EventNotes:
The Gorey Hollows features some of the SKOV (Southwest Kingdom of Vermont’s) most scenic (and gnar) ATB riding.  Plus ya know, Class 4 roads which are dirt roads that are not generally maintained and sorta left to fall to pieces. Poultney’s road maintenance budget is basically non-existent, so our class 4 roads are wonderfully terrible.  Expect wash outs, ‘gravel’ the size of GMO grapefruits, steep hike a bike grades and wonderful views. The ride weaves in and out of the woods and farm lands.  Plenty of climbing but lots of great eye candy, like cows and red barns.  

4 ride options for ‘26.  There's the classic brutal 90 mile ATB race, with the rocky class 4 roads and extended hike a bikes, the 60 mile Scramble (pick any two of the ATB race loops) and the Ramble (pick any 1 of the ATB race loops). We also have added in an ‘Amble’ ride, for folks who wanna get out and enjoy the changing seasons but don't want to walk up some terrible climb or do huge miles.  Finally, we're making the ‘Just hanging out’ option permanent.  If you or your friend / partner / etc wants to just come, drink some good coffee, eat a donut, and chow down on some dinner, this is the category for you.  More info on the ride options at the bottom of these notes. 
 

All Routes are self navigated with minimal or no sag.  You'll get a GPS track and some notes, that's it.  No sag, no medical support, nothing but a nice camp fire to come back to and some good food.  

All Analog events are rain or shine.  If you think you can't make it, get the event insurance, it's only a few bucks.  No refunds for cancelations.  It's like a concert, not a dinner reservation.   

If you are racing, your race fee gets you dinner, but not breakfast, cause no one is eating anything at 4am.  If you are doing any of the other categories, your entry fee gets you a pour over coffee, a handmade donut, and a big autumnal dinner spread from our friends at the Poultney Pub.

A note about camping: in the past, we've had folks sign up for camping thru bikereg.  This year, we're doing the camping registration thru hip camp.  It'll cost you less if you're in a group or even if there is just two of you.  We'll email info about camping sign ups to you as soon as you register.  

In the spirit of Choose Your Own Adventure books (originally published in Vermont!) you decide your destiny.  Three possible loops.  Racers have to do all 3, but pick the order of the loops.  Scramblers pick any 2 and choose the order.  Ramblers pick one.  Loops start and end at the sugar house HQ, so you can restock on water, food, clothing. 

The Amble is 15ish miles. Dirt roads, a rail trail, a class 4 road, one big hill. It's doable, chill, you can use any bike that isn't a road bike, more or less. Ideally 38mm plus tires and low gearing. James will be leading this ride, very slow group pace.

The Ramble is 30ish miles, dirt roads, plenty of climbing, bushwacking, singletrack and some sketchy class 4 roads.  Doable on a bike with decently low gearing and 50mm tires.  One of the loops has less than 4k of climbing, most ramblers will probably want to do that.  This is a very hard 30 miles. It took ramblers over 5 hours last year. Self Navigated.

The Scramble is 60ish miles.  Very difficult, even if you pick the easiest loop and one of the two hard loops.  Many riders will not finish the scramble.  You need to bring lights in case you get caught in the dark.  Lots of folks will not finish the 60 miles before sundown.  Self Navigated.

The Race is 90ish miles, with around 13,000 feet of climbing.  Singletrack, horrible rocky roads, check points, hike a bikes, and other sketch delights.  Hardest, most ridiculous ATB ride you'll ever do, we bet.  1 rider finished the race last year, out of a field of 25 or so.  Starts early.  Totally self supported old school race.   Winner gets a nice alloy ATB wheelset, second place gets pie and third some donuts.  You have to do all 3 loops to win, in any order.  Loops are directional. You can pick which to start with but you have to do them in a set direction. Self Navigated.

Rules for 2026 race: 

  • To podium, the following stuff is banned:  Aero Bars, Suspension forks, suspension frames, suspension Seatposts and stems.  E bikes are of course banned.  You can race with any of this stuff, but your results will not count toward the official record.
  • Mandatory Race time cuts so we are not up till 11pm waiting for you to come back.
  • One bike, one set of wheels and tires.  No swapping bikes like it’s a cross race.
  • Racers can refuel, change clothes, take naps, at Analog HQ in between loops.
  • Mandatory check in after every loop.  

The Gorey Hollows is a different kinda ride.  No ride leader.  No sag wagon.  It's more like a free for all with a common course and goal.    These roads are impassable to all but the most modified jeeps.  Nothing is marked.  You have to use your cue sheet and a GPS track to make it through.That's not impossible, but you have to pay attention.  There won't be any cell service for most of the ride. We will release the GPX track a few days before the race via email. 

Pre Ride Stuff: 

Racers: get here at 4:00, race starts at 5am.  Scramblers:  Leave at 8am.  Ramblers: Leave at 10am.  Amblers leave at 11am. Donuts and coffee at 7:30am and 9am

Equipment requirements for 30, 60 and 90 mile ride:

  • Sturdy walking shoes
  • Low enough gearing to make it up 15% grades that are loose and wet
  • Spare tubes/tubeless patch kits
  • Tire boots
  • GPS or Phone with GPS ability with some sort of back up battery situation.
  • Ride with GPS or GAIA.
  • 1.75" / 44mm wide tires or bigger.  Advise 2.25 or bigger.  Most past winners rode 2.8” tires.
  • Basic tools and bike repair know-how in case you break down
  • First Aid stuff.
  • There are no sag wagons!  There is no way to get out of the woods!  Be safe.  Ride Smart.

Post ride:  

Fire pit hangs at the old Analog Sugar House.  Cheer on racers as they finish laps and become more and more worn out! Autumn Feast provided by our friends at Poultney Pub.  If you saw the taco scene at the 4x4 you know these will be good.  Optional camping at the Analog HQ as well.  We’ll have some refreshments, but mainly this is a BYOB kinda deal.

Pack your bags, load your bicycle, and pedal yourself to Basecamp Flint Hills for an exclusive group campout just for bikepackers.  This is year five of our popular, self-supported, create-your-own-route bikepacking event.  

Unlimited route options via rail-trail, gravel or pavement allow you choose your own adventure. Ride solo or hook up with some folks from a local cycling community. This is a great opportunity to test out new gear and compare stories with other adventure seeking cyclists.

The Tucker Tour is what you get when you connect all of the amazing Class VI roads in and around Mount Kearsarge and Ragged Mountain in beautiful central New Hampshire. What is a Class VI road you ask? Well, the state of NH defines a Class VI road as an existing public way that has “not been maintained and repaired by the town in suitable condition for travel thereon for 5 successive years or more.”

What does this mean for those of you looking to tackle the Tucker Tour? Well, you can expect every sort of terrain, from paved and gravel roads all the way to completely unrideable hike-a-bike paths through the woods and everything in between. The 80 mile course has only 15 miles of paved roads and around 38 miles of unmaintained Class VI. Many of these paths are quite steep, which only adds to the difficulty. In summary, this is a ride that is much harder than its distance might indicate.

 

If the 80 mile course seems a bit much, there is a 62, 36, and a 24 mile course as well.  We strongly suggest loading multiple routes on to your computer/phone in case you start on the 62 mile route, but don’t have great legs and need to switch to the 36 mile route.

 

This is a 100% self-supported ride. Each participant is expected to be able to navigate on their own using the provided .gpx route or Strava route. There is no cue sheet and no navigational aids along the course. As far as provisions go, there are 2 general stores/gas stations along the route at approximately 19 miles and 54 miles.

So, what do you get for participating?  Besides the satisfaction of completing something that is incredibly hard, each participant will receive a sticker and a mug featuring this year’s unique logo design!

 

We will also be hosting a casual post-ride get together starting at 5:00 pm.  Pizza and beverages will be served, however, if you want to bring a post ride treat to share with your fellow participants, you are more than welcome to do so!

You can find more information, including a FAQ section, at lioncreekdesign.com/tucker-tour-26.

A big shout out to Josh and the Class VI Classic for showing the way.  So much of this ride is inspired by what he has put on up in Etna, NH.  If you think you would enjoy the Tucker Tour, you would have a great time in June at the Class VI Classic.

The Pisgah Mountain Bike Adventure Race (PMBAR) is the absolute pinnacle of MTB Adventure Racing. A mix of brutal and beautiful, this test of spirit and camaraderie tasks teams of two racers to reach 4 of 5 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish as fast as possible. The team with the lowest overall time wins. Checkpoint locations remain secret until start-time and there is no suggested route. Routes vary between 50-80 miles, include 9,000-15,000 feet of climbing, and take 7-14 hours to complete.

PMBAR is held deep in the Pisgah National Forest, one of the most beautiful, rugged, and unforgiving areas in the nation. There will be little to no water or food support on course. Once you leave the start/finish you are on your own. There will be no drops, sag wagons, or other outside support available. Be prepared for any circumstances you may encounter including, but not limited to: medical emergencies, navigational errors, inoperable equipment, wild animals, and stinging/poisonous insects and plants.

 

SCHEDULE OF EVENTS:

Friday 5PM-10PM – SIGN-IN OPEN 

Saturday 5:30AM-7:30AM -SIGN-IN OPEN 
Saturday 7:45AM – Mandatory Racer Meeting
Saturday 8AM – Race Start
Saturday 10PM – Race Final Cutoff

RULES:

1. Have Fun!
2. READ and UNDERSTAND the RULES. Ignorance of the rules is no excuse.
3. Team members must stay together at all times.
4. Teams must have their bikes and all other required gear at all times.
5. Approved cycling helmets must be worn at all times while riding.
6. Checkpoints may be reached in ANY ORDER.
7. Teams must reach FOUR (4) out of FIVE (5) checkpoints TO FINISH.
8. Teams that reach FIVE (5) checkpoints will be awarded a TWO (2) HOUR time bonus.
9. There will be required gear checks on course. Teams will receive a TWO (2) HOUR time penalty for each piece of missing required gear.
10. The team with the LEAST OVERALL TIME (after bonuses and penalties) WINS!!!
11. USE of OFF-MAP and HIKING-ONLY trails is STRICTLY PROHIBITED.
      A. Racers are required to use the Pisgah Map Company – Pisgah District map.
      B. Racers may NOT use other online maps or applications (i.e. Trailforks).
13. NO BUSHWHACKING. Stay on approved trails and roads.
14. Electric Assist ('E') Bikes are prohibitted.
15. RACE CUTOFF TIME: 10:00PM
16. SIGN-IN and return your TIMING CHIP upon completion of the event. PLEASE, THIS INCLUDES DNF teams. 
17. The Race Director reserves the right to disqualify any team for any reason.

VENUE:

Sign-in and Start/Finish will be in the field directly across US276 from Davidson River Campground in Pisgah Forest, NC.

OTHER:

1. PLEASE DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE THE EXTREME DIFFICULTY OF THIS EVENT.
2. We have very limited parking. Please consider leaving your car someplace other than the start/finish. For example, there are a few very large lots at the intersection of NC276 and NC280. We will also be directing half of all vehicles that arrive to the Ranger Station. Please be prepared for that possibility. Please show up early.
3. All gravel roads used in the Pisgah Mountain Bike Adventure Race will be OPEN to vehicle traffic. Please use common sense while on gravel roads. Stay to the right. Do not cut corners. Pass with care. Ride single file.

SPONSORS:

Come and enjoy miles on miles of gravel roads around beautiful Wellsboro, Pennsylvania home of the PA Grand Canyon! We have another fresh course for 2026, a few roads overlap from previous years courses and we are changing the direction of travel on some favorite roads from years prior. This route, like every year, is a BEAST!

The Full MAMMOTH course is 132 miles and roughly 13,000 ft.+ of elevation gain to challenge even the most advanced riders. Those of you that choose to attempt the Full MAMMOTH will ride two separate non overlapping loops. Both loops begin and end at the same place in downtown Wellsboro. The morning loop is 64 miles in length and afternoon is 68 miles. 

Half MAMMOTH riders will just ride the 64 mile morning loop along with the Full MAMMOTH riders but will be done riding after the morning loop.

New for this year! The Quarter MAMMOTH Route is an abbreviated version of what the half MAMMOTH Route riders are doing. You still get breakfast and lunch as well as stopping at Aid 1 for Espresso and baked goods but you only ride 39 miles and climb about 3700 ft. Not necessarily "beginner friendly" but still a challenge without absolutely destroying yourself.

Roughly halfway through each loop there will be an absolute banger of an aid station. We work with local businesses to provide hearty food at aid stations, as well as the essentials. The morning aid stop is included with all registrations. The afternoon stop is included with only Full MAMMOTH Registrations.

(Please keep in mind that there will be a support vehicle patrolling the course as well as sweep riders bringing up the rear but we highly recommend that you carry what you need for approx. 35 mile stretches)

*THIS EVENT WILL HAPPEN RAIN OR SHINE.  We DO NOT offer refunds or deferrals as all the event food and promotional items are paid for and ordered ahead of time. PLEASE CONSIDER ADDING REG INSURANCE OFFERED THROUGH BIKEREG IF YOU ARE WORRIED ABOUT WEATHER ETC. AND GETTING REFUNDED.

*We try our best to mark this monster route but the weather the previous days to the event really can dictate how well it is marked. The safest option is to use a bicycle computer with navigation or a phone app like Komoot or RWGPS for navigation. A GPX file will be sent to the email you use to register a few weeks prior to the event.

Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner will be provided for the Full MAMMOTH riders. (Options are selected in the registration process.) 

Breakfast and Lunch is included for the Half and Quarter MAMMOTH riders. (Options are selected in the registration process) 

There will be Vegan options available at all meals and aid stations.

All event day check in, meals, and after ride hang out will all be centralized around the tent constructed on the grass lot on the corner of Main St. and Central Ave. next to Beck's Bistro.

Free parking is available within a few hundred feet of the event center. If you stay at the Hotels located in downtown Wellsboro you will only be about a 2 minute bicycle ride from the Start/Mid/Finish.

If you have any additional questions please feel free to email us or PM us on Facebook or Instagram also keep an eye out on mammothendurancegravel.com for resources and information.

Tulane Cycling & Triathlon is a non-profit club sports program serving Tulane students, faculty, staff, alumni, and supporters in the New Orleans area. The club promotes all forms and levels of cycling and triathlon, with a keen focus on collegiate competition. Joining the club is easy! If you have any questions, don't hesitate to contact us.

  1. First, go to WaveSync, log in (or create a new account if you don't already have one), navigate to and fill out the Assumption of Risk Form.
  2. Register and pay your annual membership dues online here at BikeReg.
    Dues are $300/yr for either cycling and/or triathlon (and includes free Tulane Club Swim membership!). Alternatively, payment by check can be given to a club officer if necessary. Dues include a team jersey, bottle, and other goodies for every member! This includes access to our sponsors' giveaways, discount programs, etc.
  3. Join our group chat on Discord and put a photo of yourself and a little blurb in the #introduce-yourself channel.
  4. Then, come to our next meeting/ride/event. These are announced in the Discord.

Members get special discounted pricing on Tulane Cycling & Tri gear - The new kit order deadline will be announced in the fall. There is usually a second kit order early in the new year.

The Short Line Shuffle-18 Mile:

Saddle up for a laid-back ride on The Short Line Shuffle – 18 Mile. Designed for riders who want to soak in the scenery without the strain, this out-and-back course offers a smooth and approachable introduction to gravel riding.

With just around 90 feet of elevation gain, this route keeps things gentle and enjoyable, making it perfect for beginners, families, or anyone looking for a relaxed spin. You’ll cruise primarily along the scenic Cowboy Trail, where wide-open skies and peaceful stretches of Nebraska countryside set the tone for a true prairie experience.

Midway through your journey, you’ll roll into Battle Creek for a convenient stop—an ideal chance to rest, refuel, and take in a bit of small-town charm before heading back the way you came.

Whether you're new to gravel or just in it for a calm, easy ride, The Short Line Shuffle delivers a welcoming adventure with just the right touch of cowboy spirit.

 

Tracks and Tread 50K:

 

Saddle up for the heart of the Cowboy Gravel Grinder with the Tracks and Tread 50K—a perfect blend of scenic cruising and rewarding effort. This 50-kilometer route delivers approximately 500 feet of elevation gain, offering a smooth yet engaging ride for gravel cyclists of all levels.

Rolling out from the brewery, riders will head south into Nebraska’s wide-open countryside, where quiet gravel roads stretch across gently rolling terrain. Expect sweeping views, fresh country air, and the rhythmic crunch of gravel beneath your tires as you find your pace.

The route leads you toward Battle Creek, guiding you through a landscape that feels both rugged and peaceful. With manageable climbs and long, flowing stretches, this course is designed to keep you moving while still giving you time to take in the surroundings.

After reaching the turnaround, you’ll retrace your path back north, finishing where it all began—at the brewery—where a well-earned drink and camaraderie await.

Whether you're pushing your limits or enjoying the ride, the Tracks and Tread 50K captures the spirit of gravel riding: freedom, grit, and just the right amount of adventure.

 

The Frontier Fondo - 100K Route

Saddle up for the ultimate prairie adventure on The Frontier Fondo, the signature 100K route of the Cowboy Gravel Grinder. Rolling out from the brewery, riders head south into the heart of wide-open country, where the gravel stretches endlessly beneath big Nebraska skies.

With roughly 1,300 feet of elevation gain, this route offers a perfect balance of challenge and flow—long, steady rollers, punchy climbs, and rewarding descents that keep your legs working and your spirit soaring. Along the way, you’ll wind through quiet country roads, pass through charming small towns, and take in sweeping scenic views that define the frontier landscape.

Expect a ride that feels both rugged and welcoming—where every mile tells a story, every hill reveals a new horizon, and every turn reminds you why gravel riding is as much about the journey as the finish line.

The Frontier Fondo isn’t just a ride—it’s a full immersion into the soul of gravel country.

EventNotes:
Starrucca Crossing is back again for 2027 from the creators of Lu Lacka Wyco Hundo. This is the most remote course we have come up with that takes riders into some of the beauty of the Endless Mountains/Northern Tier of Pennsylvania. We start in the two stoplight town of Montrose, Pa and head right out onto gravel roads through farms, along creeks, and up and down valleys. We visit the towns of Montrose, Hop Bottom, Brooklyn, and Nicholson each with their own unique history. Come check out our 30, 50, 75, and 100 mile routes on Ride with GPS. 

The ride has full support in terms of rest stops, roving mechanics/SAG and some great pizza and drinks at the Montrose VFW when you are done. 

Due to the lack of road signs (particularly on the secondary roads) and poor cell phone signal reliability, use of GPS (downloaded and saved to your device in advance) is essential. 

What is  Your CANCELLATION POLICY? 

No refunds, No exceptions.

We begin planning, permitting,  and purchasing items for an event well in advance based on your pre-registration. Therefore we have a strict no refund policy. Be aware when you decide to register. We feel like our flexible transfer and change policies should accommodate most people and situations.

  1. CVP CANCELLATION POLICY No refunds, No exceptions.
    1. 45 Days Prior to the event:  Deadline to Defer to the following year. A fee may apply. You must transfer to the same race and Category. Deferrals are good for 1 year only. You can not defer a second year. You may transfer your entry to another person if you have a deferred entry, but it must be done 30 days prior to the event.
    2.  10 Days Prior to the Event;
      1. You may transfer your entry to a different participant using the online transfer tool. Registration is transferable to the current event and year only. The deadline to Transfer is 10 days prior to the event online.
      2. You may change to a different category for a fee. The last day to make changes is 10 days prior to the ride.
      3. If there is a waitlist in your category, you may request a credit or refund if there is a person who can take your spot off the waitlist.
      4. You may cancel your entry and receive a credit valued at 30% of your entry fee to use toward any CVP event within 1 year of cancellation. You MUST cancel no less than 10 days prior to the scheduled event.
    3. 9-0 Days before the Event:  Cancellations less than 10 days prior to an event and no-shows do not qualify for a credit.
  2. Transfers and Changes 

YOU Can now edit items on your registration if you have a Bikereg Account.  Racer name, phone, address, and email. You can also change the team category or team names. 

Transfers and Category Changes must be made through your BikeReg Account. Some actions are not allowed if you register as a guest. Change fees will apply.

If you change to a lessor distance you will not receive a refund on the price difference but we will not charge you a change fee.

If you change to a higher-priced category you will pay the change fee + the price difference.

3. Participant Insurance 

We highly suggest you purchase the insurance with your registration provided by BikeReg. This is separate from our company and will cover you in case of illness,  injury, or event cancelations due to weather and other unforeseen situations.

If you purchase the insurance and have a claim, call BikeReg directly. We can not process your claim. But, if you file one it will void any rights to a credit or transfer on our end. You can’t do both.

EventName: Siskiyou Scenic Bicycle Tour 2027/ Greenhorn Gravel Grinder
EventNotes:
Yreka, CA is located 22 miles south of the Oregon border on I-5 and is the county seat of Siskiyou County. Yreka's elevation is 2,595 ft. May is very pleasant with many wildflowers, but because of the elevation and the elevations you may climb, it is always best to be prepared for inclement weather. Siskiyou County is known for the Mt. Shasta Ski and Recreation Area, the Marble Mountain & Trinity Alps Wilderness Areas, trails, camping, bicycle touring and events, fishing, river rafting, historical districts, and now also has a casino in Yreka. Our website is www.siskiyouscenic.com. This is an open course road ride event. There are potholes, obstacles, railroad tracks, vehicles, traffic lights, signs, etc. Cyclists are responsible to be alert and obey all traffic laws. This event takes place no matter what the weather is like. Cyclists not comfortable riding under these conditions should not participate in the event.

The event is May 15th and 16th, 2027. There are 8 different rides. The longest is 102 miles, all pavement with 5,902 ft. of elev. gain, and goes over Forest Mountain into and through Scott Valley then over Gazelle Mountain and back to Yreka.This is our old traditional Siskiyou Century route. Challenging but gorgeous scenery.  There is a metric century, 67 mile route, all pavement, which goes to Edgewood and then back north, with 2,303 ft. of elevation gain- the same as last year's ride.  The 40 mile, all pavement route is 1,534 ft of elevation gain through Shasta Valley. The 21 mile  all pavement ride is 1,055 ft. of elevation gain through parts of Shasta Valley and Montague. We have 2 gravel rides on Sunday May 19th sponsored by the Jefferson Mountain Bike Association. A 39 mile mostly gravel route over Greenhorn Summit with 3 good hill climbs- with 4,114 ft. of elevation gain.  And a 62 mile mostly gravel route with 6,474 ft. of elevation gain over Greenhorn Summit into Ft. Jones then over Scarface and back to the west side of Shasta Valley. There is incredible scenery on all routes.  There is a $20 discount for registering for events both days.

We have an all pavement ride of 29 to 39 miles on Sunday May 16th through Scott Valley and Quartz Valley with 1,033- 1,159 ft. of elevation gain that will start in Fort Jones at the Forest Service parking lot, and also a part gravel route on Saturday May 15th of 58 miles through Shasta Valley with 2,279 ft. of elevation gain,  so that those who only ride 1 type of bike can enjoy 2 days of riding in Siskiyou County, or maybe you want to do 1 day of pavement and 1 day of gravel. 

All rides, except the Sunday pavement ride, start and finish at Upper Greenhorn Park, on Greenhorn Rd. In Yreka. There will be a mass start with police escort through Yreka, for the Saturday rides.   Entry fees, 102 mile- $95, 67 mile-$85, 40 mile- $65, 21 mile- $35. Sunday gravel rides, 62 mile $85, 39 mile $65. The Saturday gravel ride- $75 and Sunday pavement ride- $60. There will be a $10 late registration fee after May 1st. There will be multiple rest stops with food and drinks, and sag wagon support for all the routes. There will be an end of ride meal catered and served between 11am and 4pm on Saturday and 12-4 on Sunday. It will be much different than last year's meal- better! Beer will be available for purchase at the park both days.  Event T-shirts are available for $30 each. You must complete your ride by 4pm each day or you will be picked up by the sag wagon and returned to the park. All services end after 4:30pm. 

Tent or camper van camping will be available at Greenhorn Park Friday May 14th and Saturday May 15th for $20/night per unit. There are bathrooms, but no showers on site, however showers will be available at our local YMCA for no charge. There are several RV parks in Yreka with full hook-ups for RV's.

You may pick up your packets Friday May 14th at Upper Greenhorn Park between 5-7pm, and starting at 6am on May 15th, and 7am on Sunday May 16th. If you are riding the Sunday all pavement ride, you may pick up your packet at the Forest Service parking lot starting at 8:30am, if not picked up prior to then at Greenhorn Park. 

The route descriptions and maps may be found on our website www.siskiyouscenic.com or on RidewithGPS.com under the Siskiyou Scenic Bicycle Tour 2027. This ride is put on by the Rotary Club of Yreka, and provides funds for community projects and scholarships for our graduating high school students. There will be prizes for oldest, youngest, farthest away, 1st registration and largest group in each category.

EventNotes:
The Calvins Challenge Event for 2027 - May 15-16

I am very excited to announce that the Calvins Challenge event is back again in 2027 after being an ever greater success in 2026.

I am waiting for confirmation if any events in 2027 will be WUCA NA Championships - return here for any updates.

We are also incredibly fortunate enough to have it at the same Shawnee High School location! The format for the 100 mile, 6-hr, 12-hr and 24-hr events will be the same as 2026 - utilizing a long and short loop! There will be drafting, non-drafting, and self-supported categories. For insurance issues: I must clearly state that this is not a race. Each rider is riding for personal best in their own category.

What’s New: Nicer and shorter daytime loop.

Sadly due to the continued deterioration of many sections of the original 50-mile loop I do not feel it is safe any longer. So right after the event in May I scouted, rode, and video’d some possible replacement routes. And the winner is:

The 15.0 mile daytime loop (all events): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54088467

RAAM Qualifier (RQ): Again for 2026 - Calvins Challenge 24-hour non-drafting event will be a RAAM qualifier. The RQ Standard is 380 miles for men and 350 miles for women and 60+ men.

Where is it:

The hub of the event will be the Shawnee High School (1675 E Possum Rd, Springfield, OH 45502) If you rode in Calvin’s 2016 or earlier or 2024-25 you will recognize it. The start/finish/lap timing and crew setup will be at the back of the building in the parking lots. There is traffic circle at the intersection of Selma Pike and E Possum Rd (at the NE corner of the school) - which is a welcome addition. Here is a view of that area: Yellow path indicates bike route on road and purple is timing and crew setup. Riders will come into school back parking lot off of E Possum Rd - and then turn right on to Selma Pike

Important Dates:

  • Dec 31, 2026 - Last Day for early bird registration
  • April 1, 2027 - Last Day to order a custom Calvin’s t-shirt or Jersey
  • May 14, 2027 (Fri) 5pm - Final day for online registration
  • May 14, 2027 (Fri) - 4pm - 7pm - Packet pickup and late registration
  • May 15, 2027 (Sat) - 5am-6am - event day packet pickup and late registration

Packet Pickup and on-site Registration:

New for 2027 - No more paper waivers - I will email you a link you can us electronically sign your waiver. Then about 2 weeks before the event I will email you your digital packet including your bib # and all other info about the event. All you will have to do is show up Fri from 4-7 or Sat from 6-7 to get your bike tag and your RFID tag - then ride!

Your packet up is at the Shawnee High School Football concession stand (behind the school)

  • May 14, 2027 (Fri) - 4pm - 7pm - Packet pickup and late registration
  • May 15, 2027 (Sat) - 5am-6am - Event day packet pickup and late registration                      

Awards and snacks:

Awards will be given at the finish line area after each event as soon as results can be tabulated - Estimating 15-30 minutes after last rider in

I will provide some after ride snacks and water for the riders and crew. If you would like to bring anything to share there will be some tables to put in on. I will also work on getting some food trucks there this year too!

The courses:

  • The original 50.5 daytime loop (rider’s choice) : https://ridewithgps.com/routes/7576957
    • video: https://youtu.be/5vimwlyMqGs
  • The new 15.0 mile daytime loop (all events): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54088467
    • video: https://youtu.be/BK-nGAjvYj0
  • The original 6.8 mile finishing loop:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/7576965
    • video: https://youtu.be/7wceJTSHq3I

The events: 4 UltraCycling & 3 Time Trial Events

There will be 4 UltraCycling events: 100 Mile, 6-hour, 12-hour, & 24-hour.

There will be 3 Time Trial events: 7-Mile, 15-Mile, and 50-Mile Time Trial

All events will have the following categories: gender, 5-yr age-groups, all bike types, supported or unsupported, and solo as well as 2 thru 8 rider teams. There is something for everyone! The UltraCycling events will also have non-drafting or drafting categories.

The Century will ride 6 loops of the 15.0 mile loop and 1 loop of the 6.8 mile loop, or 2 loops of the original 50.5 mile loop (at your own peril).

The 6, & 12-hour events will all ride the 15 mile loop as many times as they can. When they feel they would not be able to complete another 15 mile loop, they will transition to the 6.8 mile loop until their event time is completed.

The 24 Hour riders will also ride the 15 mile loop as many times as they can until dark. At this time they can decide to continue to ride the 15 mile loop or switch to the 6.8 mile loop. We will make the assumption that you will ride the 6.8 loop unless you tell the timer you are going to do the 15 mile. This is so we will give you the proper credit for the loop you are riding. If you decide to ride the 15 through the night, then once you cannot complete the loop before your time expires please transition to the 6.8 mile loop until your 24 hours is completed.

Each of the Time Trials events (7, 15, & 50 miles) - Each ride one lap of each of the 3 courses (described below). All riders will leave every 15 secs immediately after all the UltraCycling riders leave. Approx 7:05am

Note: For all timed events - you must complete the loop you are on when your time expires. Your average speed on this final loop will be used to determine your prorated distance for the amount of the time you rode that loop before your timed event expires. Even if you miss-judged how long it would take you to complete one of the longer loops and your time expired while you were riding one of them, complete the loop and your distance will be prorated.

Mechanicals and/or race abandonment before completing a full lap

If you have a mechanical and had to call your crew to help and had to return to the school, you must return to the spot you stopped (via vehicle is fine) and continue if you are able. If you are not able to and you must abandon, to get credit for this partial lap you must be tracking your GPS location on your phone or Garmin (type) unit. You must save this file to Strava and present it to the Event Director when you declare you have abandoned before the official end of your timed event. If you do this then the Event Director will review your Strava ride and credit you with the mileage you rode on the partial lap.

Trains or temporary road closure due to an accident:

If you get stopped by a train or temporary road closure due to an accident: you can turn around and immediately start riding the course in the opposite direction until you feel the road will be cleared when you return, then turn back around and ride back to the same spot. To get credit for any mileage ridden in this scenario - you must be tracking your GPS location on your phone or Garmin (type) unit. When the event is over you must immediately upload the file to Strava and send it to the Event Director and tell them when and where this occurred. Ideally you will hit the  lap timer at the beginning and end of your “detour” so it can be easily seen in Strava analysis..

Event protocol:

All events will start at 7:00am and will ride their respective long loop until there is not enough time to ride another loop - then they will transition to the 6.8 mile loop until their time is finished.

Non-drafting riders let all the Drafting riders go off first.

Non-drafting Rules:

If you are in any non-drafting category, you must honor the “non-drafting zone”. We have adopted the USA Triathlon (USAT) definition of this ‘zone’: as a “rectangular area seven 7 meters long (23 feet) and two 2 meters wide (6.5 feet) surrounding each bicycle”. This will provide a sufficient non-drafting area around each cyclist.

Miscellaneous:

This event is also aligning with the World Record setting standards within World UltraCycling Association (WUCA). This new format also allows all riders to ride until the very end of their timed event. Everyone will be encouraged and allowed to complete the current lap they are on until their time event expires.

** Special Note for Trikes, Handcycles, ElliptiGOs: Due to speed, time, visibility and safety concerns, you will be allowed to ride the 6.8 Mile short-loop for the entire duration of any 6, 12, or 24 hour event if you like. Just tell me you want to do this when you check-in and I’ll assign you a special category number for it in the timing system.

Follow vehicles and crew:

Only riders who choose to ride the historic 50-mile loop (at your own peril) are allowed to have a personal support vehicle somewhere on the course to assist you. These are the rules:

  1. You must provide your contact information and also have the number of the Event Director.
  2. You may not directly follow your rider as that would present a dangerous situation with so many riders on the road. If you are seen doing this during the day, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop.
  3. You may be on the course and stop at a pre-arranged location to hand off food or drink to your rider or offer any other type of assistance they need. It is best to pick one spot and stay there until your rider transitions to the 6.8 mile loop. If possible - riders should plan on  carrying enough food and drink for a 50.5 mile ride.
  4. Your rider may call you if they need mechanical aid and you may drive to, and stop anywhere on the course to offer mechanical aid as long as it is done off the road.
  5. Handoffs from the support vehicle while it is moving are not allowed. If you are seen doing this, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop. 

During the daytime loop, supported riders may have their crew set-up anywhere along the route as long as they are completely off the road and not on private property. They may also set up in the designated area behind Shawnee High School just past the start/finish timing area.

15 & 7-Mile Loop Support rules:

  • Direct follow is not allowed when your rider is on these shorts loop. If you are seen doing this, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop.
  • You may only setup rider pit areas in the High School parking lot
  • Your rider may call you if they need mechanical aid and you may drive to, and stop anywhere on the course to offer mechanical aid as long as it is done off the road.

Where to park your vehicle:

  • There is plenty of space for parking and crew setup behind the School.
  • Preference will be given to self-supported riders to set up as near as possible to the riding path.

Electricity access:

Plan on there being no electrical outlets for you to plug into. I suggest small relatively silent generators or inverters that you can run from your vehicle if you need 110V power.

Unsupported Category:

This means that you are “totally” self-supported. You cannot have anyone help you in any way. If you get in a bad way on the course and need to call for help, you must either abandon and take your mileage at that spot - or change to the Supported Category.

Awards and souvenirs:

Registration fee includes a beautiful forged Calvins medallion especially designed for this event with a 2026 insert. Recognition each event for ALL participants in drafting, non-drafting, supported, unsupported, age-group, gender, and bike categories. There will also be recognition for Overall in all main categories. Awards and recognition ceremonies will be held individually for each event as soon as the results for each event can be tabulated after completion. Award Ceremonies after each event will be held near the start/finish line (or at the Concession Stand Shelter by the football field if raining.)

Accommodations:

  • There are many hotels in and around Springfield where you can stay
  • This is no outdoor camping allowed at the school, but you can park your RV there.

Misc Info:

Both courses used will be surveyed for exact length (to the cm), and all riders will be allowed to ride until their timed event expires, therefore allowing the greatest possible distance for each participant.

WUCA and GWR time and distance records on Surveyed Calvins courses:

Because of alignment with WUCA Record attempt rules, these surveyed courses can also be used to attempt any valid time and distance WUCA record attempt. This attempt cannot however happen simultaneously with the Calvins Challenge event. Contact records@ultracycling.com for more information about a WUCA record attempt. Registration for this must be done at least 21 days prior to your record attempt to allow the pre-attempt documentation to be completed.

Because the courses will be surveyed for exact distance to the cm (also per WUCA Record rules) based on the shortest possible rideable distance, this may vary slightly with what your GPS unit reports. (The surveyed distance is almost always a little shorter) Your final distance will be calculated off of this survey and how many laps you have completed..

Many thanks to the Shawnee School District and especially the principal and athletic director or the High School

Lastly, we are very fortunate in that the Shawnee School District  has graciously allowed us to use their High School for our event again . PLEASE be considerate of the building and the space. Don’t try to gain access to the tracks or the school. Use the time immediately after your event (while you are waiting for the award ceremony) to remove all personal items and all trash from your support area.

Note: Great cleanup job from everyone who attended the 2026 event - You could not even tell we were there - and that is how it should be!

The Farmer's Daughter Gravel Grinder (FDGG) is “the must do spring cycling event in the Northeast.” To celebrate, we've added the Farmer's Granddaughter, a shortened route with no single track/ trail sections! Regardless of which course you ride, you'll be treated to some of the most beautiful scenery in the Northeast, with plenty of climbing, and plenty of fun descents to match. Named after the Chatham Brewery’s Rye IPA born and brewed in Columbia County in beautiful upstate New York, the ride offers a truly grand tour of northern Columbia County and surrounding areas. 

All riders, regardless of route receive  FDGG Swag  and  custom FDGG name plate There will be great food and support along the way, a meal at the finish, and if you're 21 years or older,  you can also reward yourself at the finish with a free pint of Chatham Brewery’s Farmer’s Daughter Rye IPA.

Farmer's Daughter - Course description: The FDGG course is approximately 63 miles long, with about 6,000 feet of climbing - almost entirely on dirt roads with some sections of off-road thrown in. 2 sections will be on single track trails.

A gravel bike or cross bike,  is optimal for the course, and a hard-tail mountain bike would also work well. 

The Farmer's Daughter route has 3 fully supported aid stations, portable toilets, and sweep vehicles. Be sure to carry some food and water as well as spare tubes, tools, and a pump. Be prepared for a challenging, but FUN ride!

Farmer's Daughter Course Map:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/45038404

A gravel bike or cross bike,  is optimal for the course, and a hard-tail mountain bike would also work well.

Two  fully supported aid stations, portable toilets, and sweep vehicles will be provided.  Be sure to carry some food and water,  as well as the usual spare tubes, tools, and pump. Be prepared for a challenging, but fun ride!

6th Annual Red Eagle Gravel Grinder

Sunday, May 16, 2027 – 10:00 AM Mass Start
Benefiting the Steven G. Cancer Foundation

Join us for the 6th Annual Red Eagle Gravel Grinder (REGG)—a scenic day of gravel riding through the beautiful back roads of Geneva, Ohio, all benefiting the Steven G. Cancer Foundation.

We’re excited to be back at Red Eagle Distillery for another year of great riding, great company, and great support for a great cause. Riders of all experience levels are welcome, with three route options:

  • 44-mile Classic Gravel Grinder
  • 22.5-mile Sprint Gravel Grinder
  • 12-mile Family Ride

About the Rides

  • Ride hard with friends or enjoy a relaxed cruise—your pace, your adventure.
  • All riders begin together at 10:00 AM in a mass-start, Gran Fondo-style rollout from Red Eagle Distillery.
  • Please note: This is a timed ride with posted results, but it is not a race.
  • New for 2026: Chip timing for all riders, with awards for the top three Female and Male finishers in both the 43-mile and 22.5-mile routes.
  • Expect a mix of gravel, chip seal, dirt, mud, and some pavement (about 55% gravel).
  • Gravel, cyclocross, mountain, single/fixed gear, fat tire, and tandem bikes are welcome. Road bikes are not recommended.
  • E-bikes are permitted but not eligible for awards.
  • All routes will be clearly marked; cue sheets and maps will be available.
  • Official routes will be posted on Ride With GPS:
    • Red Eagle Classic Gravel Grinder – 44 Miles
    • Red Eagle Sprint Gravel Grinder – 22.5 Miles
    • Red Eagle Gravel Family Ride – 12.5 Miles
  • Registered riders will receive Ride With GPS files the week before the event.
  • Roads are open to traffic—please ride safely and obey all traffic laws.
  • Helmets are required; front and rear lights encouraged.
  • Please respect the roads and your fellow riders—no littering.
  • Water & Fuel Stops:
    • 44-mile route: 2 stops
    • 22.5-mile route: 1 stop
  • A SAG vehicle will be on course for rider assistance.

What You Get

  • The pride of riding in one of Northeast Ohio’s premier gravel events—all while supporting AYA (adolescent & young adult) cancer patients through the Steven G. Cancer Foundation.
  • A Red Eagle Gravel beer glass for every registered rider—perfect for your post-ride beverage!
  • Post-ride celebration including:
    • One complimentary drink (yes…beer!)
    • A hot bowl of chili courtesy of Red Eagle Distillery & Black Door Tavern
    • Additional food available for purchase
  • Pre-ordered Red Eagle Gravel Grinder gear will be available for pickup on event day.

No Refund Policy

The Red Eagle Gravel Grinder is a fundraiser for the Steven G. Cancer Foundation and will be held rain or shine. We are unable to offer refunds under any circumstances.

If the event must be canceled, registration fees (minus credit card and BikeReg processing fees) will be refunded. Riders will also have the option to donate their registration to the Foundation. Any cancellation updates will be communicated to participants as promptly as possible.

Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century

The event you've always known and loved... just got even better.

Welcome to the next chapter of one of Alabama's favorite gravel traditions. The Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century is everything you've come to expect—endless quiet dirt roads, Southern hospitality, and an unforgettable day on the bike—but with an exciting new home and an even bigger finish-line celebration.

For 2027, we're moving the start and finish to Historic Downtown Opelika, where race day will kick off with the energy of a community festival. Riders and spectators can enjoy local food trucks, craft beer from Red Clay Brewing Co., handcrafted cocktails from John Emerald Distillery, live music, vendors, and a vibrant downtown atmosphere before and after the ride.

Once you're out on course, it's still the Dirty Deluxe you know and love. We'll feature a 30, 60 and 100-ish mile route that showcases the best red clay roads, rolling countryside, and scenic backroads East Alabama has to offer. Along the way, expect the same welcoming volunteers, well-stocked aid stations, and the laid-back, grassroots feel that's made this event a favorite for over a decade.

We've also added a few fun new awards, expanded post-race festivities, and several surprises we'll be announcing as race weekend approaches.

To preserve the rider experience, registration will once again be limited to 350 participants. When it's full, it's full—so don't wait to claim your spot.

The Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century is proudly produced by James Bros. Bikes, with proceeds benefiting the Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation (AARRF).

About the Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation

The Alabama Animal Rescue Resource Foundation (AARRF) is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by the owners of James Bros. Bikes after encountering countless abandoned dogs while riding Alabama's backroads.

AARRF exists to support the small, privately operated rescue organizations that work tirelessly to provide sanctuary, medical care, rehabilitation, adoption, and transportation for neglected and abandoned animals throughout Alabama. These rescues fill a critical gap in a state where animal welfare resources are often limited and many county shelter systems remain overwhelmed.

Every dollar generated through the Dirty Deluxe Dirt Road Century helps AARRF continue its mission of supporting these rescue partners and giving discarded animals a second chance.

When you register, you're not only signing up for an incredible day on some of the best gravel roads in the Southeast—you’re helping change lives, both on two wheels and four paws.
PresentedBy: Red Clay Brewery and James Bros. Bikes

EventNotes:
Race will start at 6 a.m. sharp.  Course closes at midnight.  

The course is 108 miles and features very challenging terrain, with a total of 14,500 feet of climbing.

The course is 78% unpaved.

Ride with GPS - https://ridewithgps.com/routes/50534057

The course is not marked. Participants must use Ride with GPS to navigate.  Please familiarize yourself with this course as the descents can be quite dangerous. People have died descending two of these gaps on bicycles. Please use caution on the descents. The course will also feature 22% paved roads.  

No support on course. Participants must support themselves the entire route.  The support can come in the way of you carrying all of your fuel or utilizing local stores.  NOTE: Many stores in Vermont won't be open Sunday evening so you should plan accordingly, late in the race. 

Registration / check in will be Saturday evening from 6-8 p.m. or Sunday morning from 5-6 a.m.  The race will start at 6 a.m. sharp.   

Mandatory gear - Well maintained bike, cell phone, nutrition, hydration, lights, appropriate clothing for the weather conditions, repair kit, and tools. are mandatory.  All participants must have a working blinking light the entire race. Welcome to the FINGER LAKES FRESHET! 

freshet /freSHet/ noun - the springtime rush of fresh water from melting snow.

(In 2027, routes will be in the reverse direction as previous years)

This is a casual, unofficial, unsanctioned, and unsupported gravel bikepacking ride starting and ending in Stewart Park, Ithaca, NY, homeland of the Gayogohó:no people. This is a fun, but challenging ride! Less than half the riders completed it in our first two years. We avoid traffic as much as possible in our routing, but that means you can also expect some rough gravel, some singletrack, and some steep snowmobile trails. A burly gravel bike or a svelte mountain bike would be ideal. We'd recommend knobby 38-60 mm tires. 

This ride follows the self-supported ethics of other bikepacking events like The Adirondack Trail Ride, Vermont Super 8, Catskill Bikepacking Route, or the Tour Divide – meaning it's an unmarked route, with no sag wagon, no planned feed stations, etc, but you can utilize any publicly available services. And there probably won't be anyone at the finish line other than your friends and family.

You can certainly ride fast – but we also encourage riders to go slow and ride together in groups. To this end, we've organized some group camping options around mile 70 and 90 of the longest two routes. And regardless of which route you sign up for, you can switch routes if you're feeling more or less ambitious on the day of the ride.

Riders who wish to push themselves physically and mentally may choose to do so, but will need to agree to be safe about it and be respectful of everyone they encounter en route – especially on rail trails where cyclists need to yield to all other users. If you want friends and family to be able to follow your progress in real-time, we'll have the routes on Trackleaders and facilitate SPOT rental (about $85) or the PING phone app (about $15). But riders aren't required to do this unless you want your official time posted or you hope to set an official FKT (Fastest Known Time) for a route. It's the only feasible way for us to fairly and accurately record times. As a bonus, the Trackleaders webpage holds an archived event replay for all tracked events, where you can follow along with the race and ride flow!  What a fun record!  

In years past, the event was held the first weekend in early May, but for many reasons we are shifting a few weeks later. We'll continue to update the routes to avoid muddy sections. More details on routes, parking, camping, GPS tracking, and other logistics will be sent to registered riders as the Freshet approaches.

Photos, including Rigs of the Freshet portraits, can be found on our Instagram page: https://www.instagram.com/fingerlakesfreshet/

Past results:

In 2026, out of 75 registered riders, we had 31 intrepid finishers (listed below). Full replays can be found at https://trackleaders.com/freshet26. These were the courses in 2026:

Dew Drop:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54446566

Tiny Trickle: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54433808

Swollen Stream: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54433931

Raging River:  https://ridewithgps.com/routes/50554703

 

In 2025, out of 52 registered riders, only 17 courageous riders finished (listed below). Much fun was had, despite the rain and tough conditions, and it was a beautiful green spring ride, abounding with water, camaraderie, wildflowers, plenty of mud, some sublime moments, and some challenge. Kudos to TJ, who rode from his house for a total of 190 miles! Full replay here:  https://trackleaders.com/freshet25. Also see the links on rider names for articles or videos of their 2025 Freshet experience.

Course description:
The Highlands Gran Fondo showcases some of the best riding around.  It’s hard to believe riding this good is located in such close proximity to the New York/New Jersey metropolitan area.  The Highlands area is a 1,343 square mile region of Northern New Jersey which is noted for its scenic landscape and environmental importance. Much like this ride, the area is composed of rolling farmland, hilly ridgelines, and winding roads that weave up and down the lush green mountains. As you enjoy the diversity of the beautiful terrain and scenery, the route will take you through three counties and two states. As the loop progresses so will the elevation, the gran loop will gain 8,000 vertical feet. This event is sure to expose you to roads you never thought could be tucked away so close to one of the biggest metropolitan areas in the country.

The Ridge Rider Dual Consists of 2 races: The 100 mile Pine Island Gravel Odyssey and the 50 mile Dakota Five-O.  Limited to 100 participants!  Registration will be open from October 1st through March 15th.

Please understand there are no refunds once you sign up for this race.  If you sign up for this event you are committed to doing both events, so this is a risk you will have to be willing to take! The bonus however, is that you are guaranteed a spot in the 2027 Dakota Five-0 Race.  You will also get to participate in 2 incredible grass roots races, and if you FINISH both of them, you will be awarded a custom, Dykstra Pottery Mug at the Dakota Five-0 awards ceremony!  Race transfers are allowed up until June 1st however, you must give up your spot in BOTH races and you are responsible for finding someone to take your spot.  You will also need to collect payment from whomever you are transferring your spot to!  Contact Kristi Jewett at kj@kristijewett.com to make a transfer.

The act of registering for the Ridge Rider Dual event presents risks. If an act of nature or other event beyond our control occurs and we have to cancel one or both racs, what can event participants expect?

  1. Event director decisions will be based on participant safety & environmental impact. Often times these decisions are in the hands of the land owners or agencies our events are permitted through.

  2. Event directors cannot accept the risk of a cancelled event for reasons beyond our control. Participants are respectfully requested to accept the financial risk of their individual entry and understand that you will not be refunded any portion of your entrance fee if the race is cancelled.  This is due to the fact that our fees have already been payed for all supplies and services associated with the event.  These include permits, insurance, third party vendors, administrative expenses, rental fees, awards, aid station supplies, and other related expenses.

You may change your distance for the Pine Island Gravel Odyssey however in doing so you will not be eligible for the Dual Mug.

Please visit each website and read through each events policy and race information before registering.  We want everyone to be aware of what they are signing up for to make sure there is no confusion!  The individual race tranfer/refund policy does not apply to the participants of the Ridge Rider Dual (See above policy for the Dual)  Please do not register for the Dual if you don't feel comfortable with our no refund policy.

Thanks for your support and keeping the Pedal Power dream alive!

Dakota Five-0 September 5th 2027: www.dakotafiveo.com

ABOUT

Cobb County PARKS and the North Georgia Mountain Bike Association (NGMBA) invite you to celebrate the longest days of the year at the 12th Annual Voodoo Mountain Bike Race at Allatoona Creek Park—Georgia's largest purpose-built mountain bike trail system.

Held near the Summer Solstice, Voodoo has become an annual tradition that brings the Southeast's mountain bike community together to welcome summer the best way we know how: riding bikes, telling stories, and making questionable decisions deep into a race that's delightfully longer than it needs to be.

The days are long, the trails are fast, and summer is just getting started.

Whether you're chasing the podium, chasing your riding buddies, or just chasing an excuse to spend a weekend at the trails, Voodoo has a ride for you.

The ALL-a-Toona serves up more than 40 miles of twisting singletrack and attracts some of the nation's fastest XC racers. If you've ever wondered what your legs, lungs, and mental toughness are really made of, here's your chance to find out.

Looking for a challenge that's slightly less likely to have you questioning your life choices? The HALF-a-Toona delivers plenty of technical trail, fast racing, and bragging rights while leaving a little more gas in the tank for the post-race festivities.

Not interested in suffering for several hours? The TINY-Toona is all about fun, community, and good vibes. It's perfect for kids, families, first-timers, comeback riders, and anyone who wants to be part of the action without spending several hours wondering if the course is somehow getting longer. You'll cross the same finish line, hear the same cheers, and get the same Voodoo love.

Cobb County PARKS staff, led by Program Coordinator Candace Cook, along with the crew at NGMBA and an army of NGMBA volunteers, make this whole circus possible. Every dollar raised goes right back into trail construction, maintenance, and supporting mountain biking opportunities throughout the community.

PRIZES

The Voodoo crown isn't given—it's earned.

The fastest male and female riders in the ALL-a-Toona will be crowned Voodoo King and Queen and receive handcrafted royal headgear created by local legend Ed Baltes, along with a share of the event's cash purse (to be announced).

Top finishers across multiple categories will receive prizes from our sponsors. Every participant is entered into post-race prize drawings. Just don’t disappear before the awards ceremony—you must be present to claim drawing prizes.

ROUTES

We're still putting the finishing touches on the race routes, but expect a mix of flow, speed, rocks, roots, punchy climbs, and a few moments where your bike handling skills may get an honest performance review.

Taking place near the Summer Solstice means long daylight, peak summer conditions, and maximum time to enjoy the trails.

ALL-a-Tooners will tackle some of Allatoona Creek's most notorious trail segments, including Red Baron, Voodoo, and Hocus Pocus. The HALF-a-Toona delivers many of the same thrills in a shorter, slightly more forgiving format.

The TINY-Toona is pure fun. It’s a great introduction to the event for families, young riders, beginners, returning riders, and anyone looking for a relaxed introduction to race day.

Visit ngmba.org for trail information and pre-ride opportunities. Conditions may require route adjustments up until race day—walking a feature is still considered a valid survival strategy.

Race route maps can be found in the Maps section below.

EVENT DETAILS

The Voodoo takes place rain or shine unless conditions are determined to be unsafe by the Land Manager.

Please remember that Allatoona Creek Park trails are typically closed when wet. Riders should always check ngmba.org for current trail status before traveling to the park.

Start Times:

  • ALL-a-Toona: 8:00 AM
  • HALF-a-Toona: 8:40 AM
  • TINY-Toona: 9:20 AM

Official event support concludes at 2:00 PM. Riders remaining on course after that time should be prepared to continue without event support.

Helmets are required for all participants.

FOOD & HOSPITALITY

After burning through a respectable number of calories, stick around for burgers, hot dogs, chips, cookies, cold drinks, and the traditional post-race debate about where everything started going wrong.

Nothing says summer quite like finding some shade, swapping trail stories, and calling it a day with friends.

Guests are welcome to join the meal as well. Donations to help offset food costs are always appreciated.

ON-SITE CAMPING

Turn race weekend into a full Summer Solstice experience by camping on-site Thursday and Friday nights. Extra daylight means more time to pre-ride, more time to hang out, and more time to convince yourself tomorrow’s race will feel easier than it actually will.

Camping locations are assigned during registration and space is limited—register early.

No power. No water hookups. But… Portable restrooms will be available.

COST & REGISTRATION DEADLINES

The combined ALL-a-Toona and HALF-a-Toona field is limited to 350 riders.

The race sells out every year, and there is no guarantee that additional capacity will be available once registration reaches the limit.

The TINY-Toona has no participation cap.

As always, every dollar raised is reinvested into trail construction, maintenance, and mountain biking opportunities.

Registration Opens December 1, 2026

TINY-Toona
$25 through June 16

ALL-a-Toona & HALF-a-Toona
$65 Holiday Season & New Year's Resolution Super Early Bird (December 1 – January 10)
$75 Early Bird (January 11 – May 16)
$85 Standard Registration (May 17 – June 16)

Register by June 9 to ensure your requested shirt size is available.

There will be NO day-of registration.  

GET INVOLVED

Not racing? We can still use your help.

VOLUN-Tooners are a huge part of what makes Voodoo successful. We need course marshals, registration volunteers, aid station crews, parking attendants, and enthusiastic people willing to help create a great experience for every participant.

Please use the registration process above if you'd like to volunteer.

  • Race Director: Josh Camp
  • Volunteer Coordinator: Chris Sharpe

Race Info

The Black River Grand Prix returns! Join us on Saturday, June 19, 2027 for the Black River Grand Prix weekend, a celebration of fast racing, big loops, varied terrain, and fun in the woods. The format is simple: mass start on one big lap (or two). Want to race 15 miles (25k) of the best the Center has to offer? Enter the Grand Prix. Think it's so nice you want to do it twice? Then the 50k Grand Epic is for you. And if racing isn't your thing and you just want a signed ride and a good lunch, then the Grand Tour has your name on it. 

Whatever your category, this ain’t XCO, this is VT mountain biking - flow, tech, jank, doubletrack, ski trail, and maybe even a dirt road or two - there’s something for everyone. There's even a bit of pavement at the start.

The 2026 Black River Grand Epic field will head off at 10:00am for the 25-mile Epic race featuring nearly all the riding the Center has to offer. Two loops (plus a parade lap!) of nearly all our trails in the most fun layout we can pull off. This is not sufferfest racing, this is the local's loop, routed the way the builders like to ride. 

The Grand Prix will start 5 minutes later at 10:05am for those who just want one sweet race lap. 

Five minutes later at 10:07AM the Grand Tour riders go off on a mellow cruise of the same loop. The lap never loops back into the stadium, so once you’re gone, you’re gone, though the Grand Epic racers will come back through the Upper Field after their first ~15-mile lap. 

First folks back win. The courses will look nearly identical to the 2026 Grand Prix course, with a few changes and reroutes to keep y'all on your toes. 

Check out the Race Guide! for more info about this year's event.

Pricing and Prize Purses

The Grand Prix will be $50 for open racers, $30 for U23 competitors, and $25 for juniors (ages 18 and under). The Grand Epic will be $75. The Grand Tour costs $35. 

We're still in the process of figuring out prize money. But we will have cash prizes for the top three of each gender in both distances.

We will call up podiums for the top 3 overall men and women, and the top junior (U20) boy and girl. Door draw prizes will be distributed by random draw at bib pickup.

On-site Lodging

Did you know the Center has on-site lodging with meals available? Whether you want your own private cabin, a lakeside cottage, or just a room in our Cedar Lodge dorm, we can meet your needs. A room in Cedar lodge (with three meals included) starts at just $155.
